How JATMP paces these providers, and how you can see what is left of each daily budget, is explained in Enrichment and verdicts.

docs.title: Runtime and deployment
docs.text: Variable Default Purpose JATMP_HOST, JATMP_PORT 127.0.0.1, 8000 The address and port JATMP listens on JATMP_DATA_DIR ./data Where config.json and the SQLite database live JATMP_DATABASE_URL SQLite For example postgresql+psycopg://jatmp:secret@db:5432/jatmp (install requirements-postgres.txt first) JATMP_SECURE_COOKIES 0 Set to 1 behind HTTPS, for a Secure session cookie and HSTS JATMP_FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS 127.0.0.1 Proxies that may set X-Forwarded-* headers (so the audit log shows the real client IP) JATMP_PUBLIC_URL empty The public address of JATMP, used for links in API output, webhooks and MISP events JATMP_PRIVATE_HOSTS empty Private hosts JATMP may contact, as comma-separated host names or IP ranges (ollama, misp.internal, 10.20.0.0/16). Otherwise feeds, providers, the AI and MISP can only reach public addresses; see Security JATMP_TIMEZONE UTC The time zone of the daily schedule, as an IANA name such as Asia/Jakarta. The same as Time zone of the daily schedule under Settings → General

docs.title: Daily schedule
docs.text:
Two jobs run once a day: the AI executive summary (digest_time, default 06:00) and housekeeping (housekeeping_time, default 03:30). Both times are read in the time zone set under Settings → General (schedule_timezone, or JATMP_TIMEZONE), which is UTC by default.

For a team in Indonesia, choose Asia/Jakarta (WIB), Asia/Makassar (WITA) or Asia/Jayapura (WIT), and for example 07:00 for the summary. If you enter a zone name or time JATMP doesn't recognise, it keeps the previous value. The General tab shows when both jobs will next run. Times shown elsewhere on the pages stay in UTC.

docs.title: Sharing new sources
docs.text: When you add a source, the form asks for its TLP and tells you whether its items will be shared outside JATMP. A source without a TLP counts as CLEAR, so its items are shared (up to the maximum TLP set under Settings → Sharing & API, GREEN by default). Settings → Sharing & API also shows how many sources have no TLP. See Sharing and delivery.

docs.title: Extending the knowledge base
docs.text:
You can add malware families and threat actors without touching the code. Create data/knowledge_extra.json:

{
  "malware": {"WhiteArmor": {"category": "ransomware", "aliases": ["white armor"]}},
  "actors":  {"UNC9999": {"aliases": ["some alias"], "category": "nation-state"}}
}

An actor's category is optional. It feeds the dashboard's Threat actors by type chart and can be nation-state, ransomware, extortion or cybercrime; actors without one count as unclassified.

Restart JATMP, then run python manage.py reextract so that existing items are checked for the new names.

docs.title: Data model
docs.text: All tables are SQLAlchemy models in app/models.py. Times are naive UTC (models.utcnow()); never store local times or aware datetimes. This page lists what each table is for, the columns whose meaning is not obvious from their name, and the rules the code relies on. How the tables are created and changed is described under Database and migrations.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
sources 1──* items 1──* item_entities *──1 entities 1──* enrichments
                │                            │ 1
                ├──* item_geo                ├──* entity_links (src → dst)
                │                            └──* watchlist *──1 users
users 1──* api_keys        webhooks 1──* webhook_deliveries
collector_runs   notifications   insights   audit_log   settings

docs.title: sources
docs.text:
One configured feed or account.

Column Meaning kind Collector key in collectors.REGISTRY: rss, bluesky, mastodon, x, telegram, otx, urlscan, anyrun, threatfox, ransomwarelive, misp, scamsniffer category news, social or intel. Intel sources use non-strict IOC extraction and may name families in tags. config Collector settings as JSON (url, handle, query, filter…); the keys are the collector's fields. Collectors may cache ids here (Mastodon account_id). interval_minutes, enabled Schedule (minimum 5 minutes). last_run, last_status, last_error, items_count Shown on the Sources tab. last_status is ok, error, skipped or never. tlp, redistribute Sharing rules for the source's items ("" = CLEAR unless the item has its own TLP; redistribute None = the default for the kind). country, language The outlet's country and language; empty = detect. topic "" or fraud (scam & fraud sources: a generic scam word is enough, and the source appears in the fraud section).

docs.title: items
docs.text:
One collected article, post, pulse, scan or analysis. Unique on (source_id, external_id).

Column Meaning external_id Dedup key within the source (max 512 characters; longer ids end in #sha256:<hash>). kind article, post, pulse, scan, analysis. content Plain text, at most 50,000 characters; trimmed to a snippet when the item is slimmed. tags Provider tags plus tags proposed by the AI summary (those are also listed in raw["llm_tags"]). raw Small provider metadata (tlp, sector, industries, listed_by, llm_tags…). published_at, collected_at Publication time from the provider (never in the future) and storage time. Statistics use published_at; the API's since uses collected_at. severity, severity_detail 0–100 and the reasons as [{"label", "points"}]; AI reasons carry "origin": "llm" and, from 0.11, "target" (the severity the model proposed, applied again by a re-score). tlp The item's own TLP (OTX, MISP); "" = inherit from the source. origin live or backfill (historical items do not count as trending). slimmed_at Set when the retention tier trimmed the text. lang, src_country Detected language (en, id, "") and the outlet's country. fraud_score, fraud_detail, fraud_loss_idr, fraud_victims Scam analysis. fraud_score > 0 is the definition of a scam report everywhere (pages, statistics, API). is_digest true for a newsletter or round-up that wraps several unrelated stories (Talos Threat Source, weekly recaps, podcasts). Set when the item is collected and re-set by manage.py digesttag. Co-mentions (Mentioned together with, the indicators listed for a family) skip these items, and correlation discounts them: see Trends and correlation. fingerprint, dup_of Cross-source dedup for articles. dup_of points at the original item (always an original, never another copy); every count of stories (dashboards, trends, reports) counts coalesce(dup_of, id) once; only per-outlet figures count items (see Counting rules). The feed hides copies unless Show copies is ticked. llm_summary, llm_at AI summary in Markdown.

Item.source is loaded with a join; Item.entity_links is loaded lazily, so list pages use .options(with_links()) to load all links of a page in one query.

docs.title: entities
docs.text:
Anything tracked across items. Unique on (type, value); value is normalised (lower-case hashes and domains, +62… phone numbers, bank:number accounts), display is what the UI shows.

type Notes malware, actor From the knowledge base, a pattern, a feed, a provider or the AI. category is the malware category or actor kind. cve, technique CVE ids and MITRE ATT&CK technique ids. CVE intel (KEV, EPSS, CVSS) is in meta. ip, domain, url, md5, sha1, sha256 Indicators (trends.IOC_TYPES). verdict and enriched_at come from enrichment; verdict_at (0.12) is when the verdict was last given or confirmed (IPs, domains and URLs age, see Verdicts that age); meta["analyst"] (0.13) holds an analyst's verdict, which enrichment keeps; country is the hosting country of an IP, never a target. scam_type, brand Fraud taxonomy (fraud.NAMED_TYPES). phone, bank_account, ewallet, crypto_wallet Scammer identifiers (fraud.IDENT_TYPES): personal data, never returned by the API, feeds, STIX / TAXII, webhooks or MISP; phones, accounts and e-wallets are deleted after fraud_identifier_days without mentions. sector Critical infrastructure sector key (sectors.SECTOR_KEYS).

mention_count, first_seen and last_seen are maintained by pipeline.link_entities (and by the code that removes links, which decrements the count). Entities with no mentions and no links are removed by housekeeping and by manage.py reextract. verdict is "" until enriched, then malicious, suspicious, clean or unknown.

docs.title: item_entities
docs.text:
Which entities an item mentions. Unique on (item_id, entity_id).

origin Produced by regex IOC, CVE and technique patterns in the extractor, and scammer identifiers kb Knowledge base matches (families, actors), scam types, brands and sectors heuristic A new family name found by pattern ("Zorblax ransomware"); scores lower than a known family and only trends once two sources name it feed Structured indicators and family tags supplied by the feed llm Proposed by the AI summary; shown with an AI badge

manage.py reextract deletes and rebuilds the regex, kb and heuristic links and keeps feed and llm ones.

docs.title: item_geo
docs.text: The countries (and Indonesian provinces, ISO 3166-2 in region) an item is about: victims or the place where something happened. Attacker origin and hosting location are deliberately not stored here. origin is text or feed.

docs.title: entity_links
docs.text: Relationships between entities found by providers (hash → family, ip → domain). Unique on (src_id, dst_id, provider). relation is attributed-to, related, exploits…; provider decides whether the link may be shared (sharing.REDISTRIBUTABLE_PROVIDERS).

docs.title: enrichments
docs.text: One row per entity and provider with that provider's last answer (verdict, score, summary, permalink, data with tags and family labels). Unique on (entity_id, provider). Provider details only leave JATMP when api_share_provider_details is on.

docs.title: insights
docs.text: AI output that is not attached to an item or entity: kind digest (executive summary, structured fields in data) or answer (Q&A, deleted after 90 days).

docs.title: Users and access
docs.text: Table Notes users role is viewer, analyst or admin (auth.ROLES, ordered). Single-user mode uses a built-in local user (auth.LOCAL_USER) that cannot log in. session_version is bumped by auth.end_other_sessions(); cookies with another version are rejected. notif_read_at is the notification read watermark. api_keys prefix (public part), secret_hash (SHA-256 of the secret, never the secret), scopes (read, export, write), expires_at, revoked_at, last_used_*. watchlist Entities a user watches (entity.watched webhook, watchlist page). audit_log Who did what (audit(db, user, action, detail, request)), with the client IP. corrections Analyst corrections (0.13): kind (unlink, false_positive, verdict, not_scam), item_id / entity_id, value (the verdict), reason, who and when, active until undone (undone_at, undone_by), and in data what it changed (removed links with their origin, the previous verdict) for the undo and the quality report. See Corrections and quality.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text: Table Notes collector_runs One row per job run. job is source:<id>, backfill:<id>, enrichment, cve_intel, geotag, fraudtag, rescore…; status is queued, running, ok, error, skipped or aborted; batch_id groups the runs of one manual action (collect-…, backfill-…); progress_* and phase are copied from the in-memory progress when the run finishes. Deleted after 30 days. notifications user_id None = everyone; key de-duplicates (the same key is not written twice); link is a same-origin path. webhooks, webhook_deliveries Hooks store a salt, not a secret: the signing key is derived from the install secret. Deliveries are pending, ok or failed, with attempts and next_attempt_at for the back-off.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
settings is a key–value table (key, JSON value). Every key is declared in settings.SCHEMA as (default, env var, label, kind, group):

  • settings.get(key) returns the environment variable when one is set (the UI then shows the field as locked), else the stored value, else the default. Values are cached for 5 seconds.
  • kind is text, int, bool, secret or select:a,b,c. int values are clamped by INT_BOUNDS when saved from the UI.
  • Values of kind secret are stored as enc:v1:<Fernet token>. The key is derived from secret_key in data/config.json, so a database without its config.json cannot decrypt them (they then read as empty).
  • Keys that are not in SCHEMA are internal state: rules versions (fraud_version, geo_version, sector_version, content_version, dedup_version, digest_version), netguard_seeded, provider daily budgets, the builtin sources already offered.

data/config.json (not in the database) holds what must exist before the database does: installed, mode (single or multi), app_name, secret_key (session signing, webhook signatures, settings encryption) and database_url.

docs.title: Development
docs.text: How to set up a development environment, run JATMP locally without touching real data, write and run tests, manage dependencies, and release a version. How the code is organised is in Architecture, the tables in Data model, and recipes for common changes in Extending JATMP.

docs.title: Set up
docs.text:
Requirements: Python 3.11 or 3.12, git. Docker is optional (only to test the image).

git clone https://github.com/fj4rr/just-another-threat-monitoring-platform.git

cd just-another-threat-monitoring-platform

python -m venv .venv

Activate the virtual environment (source .venv/bin/activate, or .venv\Scripts\activate on Windows), then install the pinned dependencies and the development tools:

pip install -r requirements-dev.txt -c requirements.lock

Optional extras: requirements-postgres.txt (PostgreSQL driver), requirements-telegram.txt (MTProto), requirements-docs.txt (documentation site).

docs.title: Run locally
docs.text:
python run.py

This serves on http://127.0.0.1:8000 and starts the scheduler, which collects from every enabled source. Useful variations:

  • Throw-away data. JATMP_DATA_DIR decides where config.json and the SQLite database live. Point it at an empty folder to get a fresh install (the setup wizard opens) without touching data/:

    JATMP_DATA_DIR=/tmp/jatmp-dev python run.py --port 8001

    On Windows PowerShell set $env:JATMP_DATA_DIR first. Uncheck Add default sources in the wizard if you do not want collectors to start fetching. - Auto-reload. python run.py --reload restarts on code changes. The scheduler restarts with it, so scheduled runs may start again after each save. - No collectors. To look at pages without network traffic, install without default sources, or disable the sources under Settings → Sources. - Seeding test data. Import the app with the same JATMP_DATA_DIR in a script and call pipeline.ingest(db, source, [RawItem(...)]) inside db.session_scope(); the pages show the result at once. - A local AI. Run Ollama and choose Local – Ollama under Settings → AI. Saving the AI tab in local mode adds the host to the outbound allow-list.

The interactive API reference is at /api/v1/docs once you are signed in.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Python 3.11+, from __future__ import annotations at the top of modules, type hints on public functions.
  • Lint: ruff check . must pass (rules in pyproject.toml: pycodestyle, pyflakes, isort, bugbear, pyupgrade, bandit, naming, comprehensions, simplify, ruff). Line length is 120. Fix findings instead of silencing them; a # noqa: XXX needs a reason in the same comment.
  • Comments explain why, not what: the incident, the false positive or the provider quirk behind a rule. Rules that came from an audit or an issue name it ("audit 2026-11 D-1").
  • Times are naive UTC from models.utcnow().
  • The UI and the docs are in English. Indonesian appears in detection patterns and in names.
  • No new dependency without a reason: the app runs on small hosts and offline. Front-end code stays build-free; third-party JavaScript is vendored under static/js/vendor/.
  • Security rules for every change are listed at the end of Extending JATMP.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
pytest

pytest tests/test_v0101.py -k identifiers      # one file, tests matching a name

pytest -x --lf                                 # stop at the first failure, rerun what failed last time

How the suite works:

  • tests/conftest.py sets JATMP_DATA_DIR to a fresh temporary folder before importing app, and removes provider keys from the environment, so tests never see your data or your keys.

  • Fixtures:

    Fixture Gives you installed A single-user install with the default sources, once per session client A TestClient for the app without the lifespan (no scheduler, no collectors) multi_user_mode Switches the install to multi-user for one test and provides an admin (admin / password in the fixture) _fresh_caches (autouse) Clears the trending cache and the manual-action throttles before each test

  • One database for the whole session. Tests add data with names that do not collide (Zz…, zz-… prefixes) and assert on their own rows rather than on totals.

  • No network. Replace HTTP clients with httpx.MockTransport: monkeypatch Collector.client, intel.clients._client, intel.context._client, intel.darkweb._client, or pass http= where a function accepts one (cve.refresh, webhooks.deliver_pending). Tests of netguard itself use a local ThreadingHTTPServer.
  • CSRF in tests. Read the token from a page (<meta name="csrf-token">) and send it as X-CSRF-Token or csrf_token; see the _csrf helper in the test files.
  • Files per release. New behaviour goes into the file of the release that introduces it (test_v0101.py…); core behaviour lives in test_app.py, test_extractor.py, test_scoring_and_reports.py and test_security_units.py.
  • Numbers in the docs. tests/test_docs_numbers.py reads the weights, thresholds, windows and defaults that the How it works pages quote and compares them with the constants in the code. A change on one side only fails the build; fix the page or the code, and add a check when a page quotes a new number that matters.
  • What to test. For a detection rule: the case that motivated it, the false positive it must not produce, and an existing true positive that must still match. For a security fix: the attack. For a regular expression that is not trivial: a timing test with hostile input.

GitHub Actions (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs on every push and pull request:

Job What test ruff check . and pytest on Python 3.11 and 3.12, dependencies from requirements.lock audit pip-audit against requirements.lock (known vulnerabilities fail the build) docker Builds the image

.github/workflows/docs.yml builds and publishes the documentation site.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
• requirements.txt lists direct dependencies with compatible ranges (>=x,<y). It is what pyproject.toml reads.
  • requirements.lock pins every package, direct and transitive, for all platforms. Docker and CI install with -c requirements.lock.
  • Dependabot (.github/dependabot.yml) proposes updates weekly; merge them when CI is green.

To add or update a dependency, edit requirements.txt, then regenerate the lock with uv and check it:

uv pip compile requirements.txt --universal --python-version 3.11 -o requirements.lock --no-header --upgrade

pip-audit -r requirements.lock

pip install -r requirements-dev.txt -c requirements.lock && pytest

Drop --upgrade to change only what the edit requires. Keep upper bounds loose enough that a security fix can be installed (a bound below the fixed version makes pip-audit fail).

docs.title: Documentation site
docs.text:
The pages under docs/ are plain Markdown that reads on GitHub and also builds a MkDocs (Material) site, published to GitHub Pages by .github/workflows/docs.yml on every push to main that touches the docs.

pip install -r requirements-docs.txt

mkdocs serve                  # http://127.0.0.1:8000 with live reload

mkdocs build --strict         # what CI runs: broken links and anchors fail the build

Navigation is in mkdocs.yml; add a new page there and to the index in docs/README.md. scripts/mkdocs_hooks.py renders the root CHANGELOG.md as the changelog page and rewrites the links that only make sense on GitHub (../CHANGELOG.md, ../README.md, the "← Documentation index" back links). Screenshots live in docs/screenshots/; retake them when a page changes visibly (see Screenshots).

Which page to update:

Change Page New source kind or default source Sources New provider, key or environment variable Configuration Detection, scoring, enrichment Analysis, Scams and fraud, Geography API, feeds, webhooks, MISP Sharing and integrations Anything security-relevant Security New table or column Data model New module, job or flow Architecture Anything an admin must do after upgrading Upgrading

docs.title: Release checklist
docs.text:
1. Bump the version in app/__init__.py (__version__, shown in the UI and the API docs) and in pyproject.toml.
  2. Rules changed? Bump the matching version constant so stored items are re-analysed once (see Background jobs).
  3. Add a section to CHANGELOG.md (what changed, from the user's point of view) and to docs/upgrading.md (what an admin has to do or should expect: new columns, one-off jobs, new dependencies, changed defaults).
  4. Update How it works (docs/how-it-works/) for every changed rule, weight, threshold, interval or job, and the checks in tests/test_docs_numbers.py when a quoted number moved or a new one was added.
  5. Rules changed? Run python manage.py quality. If an area got better, record it with python manage.py quality --update-baseline and put the new precision / recall in the changelog; if one got worse, tests/test_quality.py fails until the rule or the case is fixed. See Corrections and quality.
  6. Run ruff check ., pytest, pip-audit -r requirements.lock and mkdocs build --strict.
  7. Try the upgrade path: copy a data/ folder from the previous version, start the new version on the copy (JATMP_DATA_DIR), and check the start-up log and the one-off jobs.
  8. Commit, push, and check that CI is green (the job summary shows the quality report).

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause Every page redirects to /setup JATMP_DATA_DIR points at a folder without an installed config.json A source fails with blocked: … resolves to a private or local address The outbound guard; add the host under Settings → Sharing & API → Private hosts JATMP may contact Stored API keys read as empty The database was moved without its data/config.json (the key that decrypts them) database is locked on SQLite A long write transaction; commit in chunks, or use PostgreSQL for heavy backfills Collectors run twice More than one worker or process is serving the app A test passes alone and fails in the suite It depends on totals or on data another test added; assert on your own rows

docs.title: Extending JATMP
docs.text: Recipes for the changes developers make most often. Each one names the files to touch, the code to write, the rules to keep and the tests to add. Read Architecture first for how the pieces fit together, and Development for setting up, testing and releasing.

docs.title: Add a collector (a new kind of source)
docs.text:
A collector turns one provider into RawItems. It does not touch the database: storing, extraction, scoring and linking happen in the pipeline.

  1. Create app/collectors/<name>.py:

    from __future__ import annotations

from .. import settings
from ..processing.pipeline import RawItem
from .base import Collector, SkipCollector, parse_dt


class ExampleCollector(Collector):
    """Latest reports from example.org. One sentence on what it collects and what it needs."""

    kind = "example"           # stored in Source.kind; never change it once released
    category = "intel"         # news | social | intel
    label = "Example reports"  # shown in the "Add source" form
    # config fields for the UI: (name, label, placeholder); values end up in Source.config
    fields = [("query", "Search query", "ransomware")]

    def fetch(self) -> list[RawItem]:
        key = settings.get("example_api_key")
        if not key:
            raise SkipCollector("Example API key not set (Settings → Threat-intel APIs)")
        with self.client(Authorization=f"Bearer {key}") as c:  # netguard client: SSRF guard, size cap
            r = c.get("https://api.example.org/v1/reports", params={"q": self.cfg.get("query", "")})
            r.raise_for_status()
            rows = r.json().get("data") or []
        return [RawItem(external_id=str(x["id"]), title=x.get("title", ""), url=x.get("url", ""),
                        content=x.get("summary", ""), published_at=parse_dt(x.get("created")),
                        kind="pulse", tags=x.get("tags") or []) for x in rows]

  2. Register the class in REGISTRY in app/collectors/__init__.py. The settings page, the scheduler and run_source pick it up from there.

  3. Optional: add a default source to DEFAULT_SOURCES. Existing installs get new built-in sources on the next start (auto_seed_sources), so only add sources that work without configuration, or add them disabled.
  4. Optional: historical backfill. Override backfill_capability() and backfill(since, until, progress), which yields pages (lists) of RawItems newest first, calls progress("page 3") and stops at until/since. See mastodon.py for a small example and rss.py for WordPress and Internet Archive.

Rules:

  • Always use self.client(...), never httpx directly. Header keyword names use _ for -.
  • Raise SkipCollector for "cannot run, nothing is wrong" (missing key, disabled plan); let other errors raise: the run is marked as an error and the admin is notified once.
  • external_id must be stable across runs, or every run stores duplicates.
  • Put HTML into content only with kind="article" (it gets stripped); posts and pulses are plain text.
  • Put structured indicators into indicators (intel.make_ioc(value) builds them) rather than into the text.
  • Keep raw small: it is stored on every item.
  • If the provider's terms forbid redistribution, add the kind to sharing.NO_REDISTRIBUTE_KINDS.

Tests: replace the HTTP client with a mock transport and assert on the RawItems and on what ingest stores.

def test_example_collector(installed, monkeypatch):
    def handler(req: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        return httpx.Response(200, json={"data": [{"id": 1, "title": "Zzexample LockBit", "created": "2026-11-01"}]})

    monkeypatch.setattr(Collector, "client", lambda self, **h: httpx.Client(transport=httpx.MockTransport(handler)))
    settings.set("example_api_key", "test")
    raws = REGISTRY["example"](Source(name="x", kind="example", category="intel", config={})).fetch()
    assert raws[0].external_id == "1"

docs.title: Add an enrichment provider
docs.text:
Providers answer "what do you know about this indicator?". They live in app/intel/clients.py (lookups that run automatically), app/intel/context.py (on-demand infrastructure context) or app/intel/darkweb.py (deep dive).

class Example:
    name = "example"                       # stored in enrichments.provider; never change it
    supports = {"ip", "domain"}             # indicator types it can look up

    def __init__(self):
        self.key = settings.get("example_api_key")
        if not self.key:
            raise NotConfigured("Example API key not set")   # the provider is then simply skipped

    def lookup(self, etype: str, value: str) -> LookupResult | None:
        if etype not in self.supports:
            return None
        if not _budget_ok(self.name, int(settings.get("example_daily_budget") or 0)):
            raise RuntimeError("Example daily budget exhausted")
        throttle.wait(self.name, 2)          # seconds between calls
        with _client({"X-Key": self.key}) as c:
            r = c.get(f"https://api.example.org/v1/{etype}/{value}")
        if r.status_code == 404:
            return LookupResult(self.name, "unknown", 0, "Not known to Example")
        r.raise_for_status()
        d = r.json()
        return LookupResult(self.name, verdict="malicious" if d.get("bad") else "unknown", score=d.get("score", 0),
                            summary=d.get("summary", ""), permalink=d.get("link", ""),
                            malware=d.get("families", []), tags=d.get("tags", []))

    def test(self) -> str:                   # "Test" button under Settings; avoid spending lookup quota
        with _client({"X-Key": self.key}) as c:
            c.get("https://api.example.org/v1/account").raise_for_status()
        return "Example reachable, key accepted"

Then:

  1. Add it to PROVIDER_CLASSES in app/processing/enrichment.py (or CONTEXT_CLASSES in intel/context.py). The Test buttons on the settings page find providers by name in those lists.
  2. Add its settings (example_api_key, a budget) to settings.SCHEMA, see below.
  3. If its verdicts are noisy (it lists scanners and CDNs), add the name to NOISY_PROVIDERS so a GreyNoise "benign" answer overrides it in _consensus.
  4. If its relationships may be shared, add the name to sharing.REDISTRIBUTABLE_PROVIDERS.
  5. Document the key in Configuration.

malware labels are mapped to known families by enrichment.resolve_family; unknown labels are ignored on purpose, so a strange provider label never creates a family.

docs.title: Add a setting
docs.text:
Add one line to SCHEMA in app/settings.py:

"example_daily_budget": (500, "EXAMPLE_DAILY_BUDGET", "Example lookups per day", "int", "enrichment"),
#                        default  env var (or "")    label in the UI            kind   group (= settings tab)
  • The field appears on its tab automatically (settings.html renders every SCHEMA entry of the tab's group). A new group also needs a tab in the list at the top of settings.html.
  • Kinds: text, int (add bounds to INT_BOUNDS), bool, secret (never sent to the browser, stored encrypted), select:a,b,c.
  • An environment variable, when set, wins and locks the field.
  • Read it with settings.get("key"). Values are cached for 5 seconds per process.

docs.title: Change detection rules
docs.text:
Rules are data in Python modules. After changing them, update the tests that pin their behaviour, add the case that motivated the change (and a counter-example that must not change) to tests/quality/, run python manage.py quality, and decide how stored items catch up. The Most corrected list on the Corrections page is a good place to find rules worth changing; see Corrections and quality.

What Where Stored items catch up through Malware families, actors, aliases MALWARE, ACTORS in app/knowledge.py (or data/knowledge_extra.json without code, see Configuration) manage.py reextract Names that are everyday words COMMON_WORDS / AMBIGUOUS in knowledge.py: these need a qualifier ("Pegasus spyware", "Bitter APT"), unless written in a distinctive spelling (knowledge.distinctive: "RedLine", "Cl0p"); QUALIFIERS / ACTOR_QUALIFIERS list the qualifiers manage.py reextract Things that are never indicators BENIGN_DOMAINS, BENIGN_IPS (public DNS resolvers) and ABUSED_HOSTING (paste and file-sharing services: the domain never, a URL with a path always) in processing/extractor.py manage.py reextract Words that are never a new family GENERIC_WORDS, LEGIT_TOOLS, PLATFORM_WORDS, ID_GENERIC_WORDS in processing/extractor.py (country names and demonyms come from the gazetteer) manage.py reextract Severity terms and weights GROUPS and ID_TERMS in processing/severity.py, dampeners PATCH_RE, META_RE, NOISE_RE bump severity.RULES_VERSION Scam types SCAM_TYPES in processing/fraud.py: (key, name, weight, strong pattern, weak pattern) bump fraud.RULES_VERSION Brands, identifier cues, losses BRANDS, SCAMMER_SPECIFIC, SCAMMER_CUE, INSTITUTION_CUE, OFFICIAL_CUE, VICTIM_CUE, RE_RUPIAH / RE_DOLLAR in fraud.py bump fraud.RULES_VERSION Sectors SECTORS, FEED_SECTORS, ATTACK_CUE in processing/sectors.py bump sectors.RULES_VERSION Countries, provinces, places app/gazetteer.py, detection in processing/geo.py bump geo.GEO_VERSION Text cleaning strip_html / strip_css in processing/pipeline.py bump jobs.CONTENT_VERSION Topic filters (security, cyber, fraud) processing/topics.py, used by every news and social source Not at all: filters only decide what is stored from now on

Rules for patterns:

  • Linear time only. Every article goes through these regular expressions in a scheduler thread that cannot be killed. Never nest unbounded quantifiers ((a+)+, (x(?:y)?)+(?:\s*(x)+)*), never let two adjacent parts match the same text, bound repetitions ({0,40}), and add a timing test with a hostile input when a pattern is complex (see test_strip_css_is_linear).
  • English and Indonesian forms of one signal share a label, so they count once.
  • Prefer false negatives to false positives in the fraud section: a wrong scammer phone number is personal data stored without reason.
  • Write the reason a pattern exists as a comment next to it, with the example that motivated it.

docs.title: Re-analyse stored items after a rules change
docs.text:
For the rules in the table above with a version constant, bumping the constant is enough: the matching start-up job re-analyses every stored item once. For a new kind of analysis, add a job following the same pattern in app/jobs.py:

EXAMPLE_VERSION = 1  # 1 (0.11): what changed, in a few words


def run_example(force: bool = False) -> str:
    if not force and int(settings.get("example_version") or 0) >= EXAMPLE_VERSION:
        return "example is up to date"
    db = SessionLocal()
    try:
        ids = [i for (i,) in db.execute(select(Item.id).order_by(Item.id))]
        for n in range(0, len(ids), 500):          # chunks: bounded memory, short write transactions
            for item in db.execute(select(Item).where(Item.id.in_(ids[n:n + 500]))).unique().scalars():
                ...                                   # recompute and store
            db.commit()
            db.expunge_all()
        settings.set("example_version", EXAMPLE_VERSION)
        return f"updated {len(ids)} item(s)"
    except Exception as e:
        db.rollback()
        log.warning("example failed: %s", e)
        return f"error: {e}"
    finally:
        db.close()

Schedule it once in jobs.start() (scheduler.add_job(run_example, "date", run_date=_now() + timedelta(seconds=…), id="example", replace_existing=True)), mention it in Upgrading, and, if users may want to run it again, add a manage.py command and a button. Jobs that need progress in the UI create a CollectorRun (_start_run / _finish).

docs.title: Add a page
docs.text:
1. Add a route to the matching router in app/routers/ (pages in pages.py, scam pages in fraud_pages.py, admin pages in admin.py):

    @router.get("/examples")
def examples(request: Request, days: int = 30, user: User = Depends(current_user), db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    days = _clamp(days, 0, 3650)                              # clamp every number from the query string
    rows = db.execute(select(Item).options(with_links())     # with_links() when the template reads entity_links
                      .order_by(Item.published_at.desc()).limit(50)).unique().scalars().all()
    return render(request, "examples.html", {"user": user, "rows": rows, "days": days})

  2. Create app/templates/examples.html extending base.html; reuse the macros in _macros.html (chip, sev, verdict, fraud_score…). Inline scripts need nonce="{{ nonce }}"; behaviour goes through data-* attributes or static/js/app.js, never onclick.

  3. Add the link to the sidebar in base.html if it is a top-level page.
  4. Use require("analyst") or require("admin") instead of current_user when the page changes data or shows admin information.

docs.title: Add a UI action or JSON endpoint
docs.text:
Actions the UI calls with data-post live in app/routers/api.py:

@router.post("/examples/{item_id}/refresh", dependencies=[Depends(verify_csrf)])
def example_refresh(item_id: int, request: Request, user: User = Depends(require("analyst")),
                    db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    item = db.get(Item, item_id)
    if not item:
        raise HTTPException(404, "item not found")
    throttle.check(f"{user.id}:example_refresh", 6)     # when it calls a provider or the AI
    ...
    audit(db, user, "example_refresh", str(item.id), request)
    db.commit()
    return {"ok": True, "message": "refreshed"}          # shown as a toast
  • Every non-GET route needs verify_csrf.
  • Work that takes more than a second or two goes into a job (jobs.run_now(func, *args), or a queued CollectorRun so the UI shows progress), not into the request.
  • Wrap provider calls that must not run twice at once in with throttle.exclusive(f"example:{id}"): ….

docs.title: Extend the REST API
docs.text:
The versioned API is app/routers/api_v1.py. It is read-only and has its own authentication:

  • Use Depends(principal("read")) (or "export" for bulk feeds) instead of current_user.
  • Filter with sharing.shareable_item_clause() / sharing.shareable_entity_clause() and check single objects with sharing.item_shareable(); return 404 (not 403) for objects that may not be shared.
  • Never return entities of fraud.IDENT_TYPES, in lists, in single-object endpoints or nested in other objects.
  • Page with cursor (the last id) and limit, return next_cursor.
  • CSV output goes through csvsafe.writer.
  • The endpoint appears in the offline docs at /api/v1/docs automatically; give it a summary and describe the query parameters, then mention it in Sharing and integrations.

docs.title: Add a column or a table
docs.text:
1. Declare it in app/models.py. Give new columns a default (scalar defaults are applied to existing rows when the column is added), and index=True when it is filtered or sorted on.
  2. Restart: init_db() creates new tables, adds new columns and creates declared indexes on existing tables.
  3. Never rename or drop a column in a release, and never add a NOT NULL column without a default. If existing rows need a computed value, add a versioned one-off job (see above).
  4. Check the column with PostgreSQL in mind: declared string lengths are enforced there (the before_flush hook trims, but a key that gets trimmed may collide).
  5. If the data is copied between engines, check app/dbcopy.py.
  6. Describe it in Data model and the upgrade notes.

docs.title: Make outbound requests
docs.text: Use netguard.client(...) or one of the existing helpers (Collector.client, intel.clients._client). Choose max_bytes for large downloads, follow_redirects=False when a redirect would be wrong (webhooks, MISP), and allow_private= only where an admin explicitly configured a private target. Tests replace these helpers with an httpx.MockTransport client; never let a test reach the internet.

docs.title: Security checklist for a change
docs.text:
• Untrusted input: feed text, provider answers, AI output, query strings, form fields, uploaded settings. Validate and bound it; never build SQL, FTS queries, shell commands or HTML from it without escaping.
  • Templates auto-escape; never mark untrusted text |safe. Markdown goes through the md filter (raw HTML off).
  • Links from feeds go through safe_url / safe_href.
  • New outbound data paths respect sharing.py and leave scammer identifiers out.
  • New outbound requests use netguard.
  • New regular expressions are linear.
  • New secrets are secret settings, never logged and never sent to the browser.
  • Admin-only data and actions check require("admin"); changing actions write to the audit log.

docs.title: Scams and fraud
docs.text: Since 0.9 JATMP reads every collected item a second time as a possible scam report. Scam reports get their own section (Scams & fraud in the menu) but stay on the same pipeline and entity graph as everything else, so a wedding-invitation APK scam links to the Android banking trojan it installs, a crypto drainer report to its phishing domains, and an infostealer campaign to the account takeovers that follow. The International / National (ID) switch applies here too.

docs.title: What is detected
docs.text: How Scam type A fixed taxonomy in English and Bahasa Indonesia: investment scam (incl. investasi bodong, robot trading, pig butchering), illegal online loan (pinjol ilegal), job / task scam, romance scam, sextortion, malicious APK lure (wedding invitations, traffic tickets, bills), courier / package lure, impersonation, phishing, OTP theft / account takeover, online gambling (judol), fake shop, prize / giveaway (incl. fake bansos), crypto scam / drainer, tech support / refund scam, BEC / invoice fraud, QRIS / QR code fraud, deepfake scam, and Other scam. Typical phrases include fraudulent investment apps, callers who mengaku dari Bea Cukai, the police, a bank or the tax office, SMS phishing and smishing messages, fake payment or delivery pages, fake QRIS stickers, and fake sellers or jual beli … online fraud. Tools and policies against scams (aplikasi anti-scam, an anti-fraud team) are no scam word. Strong phrases count on their own; weaker ones ("phishing", "APK", "deepfake", "mengatasnamakan") only next to a scam word (within about 200 characters, or a scam word in the title), and outside fraud sources one passing scam word is not enough. An article whose title says nothing about a scam must show the scam in more than one place, so a malware write-up with one sentence about "scammers using fake delivery notices" stays out. Newsletters and weekly round-ups are judged on their title only. Impersonated brand About 70 banks, e-wallets, marketplaces, couriers, telecoms, utilities, government bodies, platforms and crypto exchanges, Indonesian first (BCA, BRI, Bank Mandiri, BNI, DANA, OVO, GoPay, Shopee, J&T, PLN, OJK, BPJS, DJP, Bea Cukai…). A brand counts when it appears next to an impersonation cue ("mengatasnamakan BCA", "fake PayPal"). A brand that speaks or acts ("Shopee warns customers…", "BCA mengimbau nasabah", "kata pihak OJK", "Coinbase blocks $4.7 million in transfers to scammers", "BRI Ajak…", a headline "Indodax: …") is not the one impersonated, unless the text says so right next to the name ("fake Shopee websites"). A brand's own advisory that names no case ("nasabah diimbau berhati-hati saat menerima komunikasi yang mengatasnamakan BRI", with no victim, perpetrator, loss or circulating fake) talks about impersonation in general and names no brand. A plain scam word only counts right next to the name ("phishing BCA", "penipuan berkedok hadiah BRI"), not a sentence away. Platforms and government bodies need the cue right next to them, because they are usually the channel ("lewat WhatsApp") or the one issuing the warning ("FBI warns…"). Ambiguous words are matched carefully: dana (funds) is not DANA, mandiri (independent) is not Bank Mandiri. Impersonated person Public figures whose name or face a scam borrows: deepfake giveaways and investment ads ("Deepfake Elon Musk", "an AI-generated deepfake of Elon Musk"), mencatut nama Menteri Keuangan Sri Mulyani, fake accounts of officials. They are brands of the type person (same lists, filters, chips and graph). A list of about 45 often-borrowed names (Elon Musk, Donald Trump, Prabowo Subianto, Sri Mulyani, Raffi Ahmad…) counts next to an impersonation cue or in a sentence about a deepfake; other names only count right after an office or calling ("mencatut nama Bupati Bandung Dadang Supriatna", "posing as billionaire …"). A name without one is left alone, because it may belong to a private person. Scammer identifiers Phone numbers (Indonesian mobile numbers normalised to +628…), bank accounts (with the bank when it is named), e-wallet numbers and crypto wallets (BTC, ETH, TRON; Bitcoin and TRON addresses must pass their Base58Check or bech32 checksum, so an invoice number is no wallet). See the rules below. Losses and victims The largest loss a report states (headline forms such as "Rp 2,5 T" and "Rp 5 M" included), converted to rupiah (dollar amounts at the rate set under Settings → Scam & fraud), and the largest victim count ("1.200 korban", "ratusan korban", "thousands of victims"). Amounts only count next to a loss word, so prices and fees are ignored, and money that was saved, frozen or returned is not a loss.

docs.title: Fraud score
docs.text:
Each scam report gets a fraud score from 0 to 100, separate from the threat severity and explained the same way (click the score on the item page, or see the side preview):

Part Points Scam type (the strongest one) 10–28, e.g. malicious APK lure 28, investment scam 26, OTP theft 24, phishing 18, online gambling 12 More scam types in the same report +4 each, up to +8 Impersonated bank, e-wallet or government body / person / other brand +10 / +8 / +6 Reported losses +5 below Rp 100 million, up to +30 from Rp 1 trillion Reported victims +5 from 10, up to +20 from 10,000 Scammer identifiers published +8 Official warning or law enforcement (OJK, Satgas PASTI, IASC, police, FBI / IC3, FTC, BSSN, arrests) +8 Spreading: at least 5 reports of the same scam type this week and twice as many as the week before +8

docs.title: Scammer identifiers and personal data (UU PDP)
docs.text:
Phone numbers and bank accounts are personal data under Indonesia's Personal Data Protection Law (UU PDP, Law 27/2022). JATMP keeps as little as it can:

  • Identifiers are taken only from items that are about a scam, and only where the sentence marks them as the scammer's (nomor penipu, pelaku menghubungi dari, transfer ke rekening, "texts from"…). A plain "hubungi nomor" or "contact" is not enough when the same sentence names an institution (Polres, kantor cabang, layanan pengaduan, OJK…): "Hubungi Polres Jakarta Selatan di nomor 0812…" is the police's number.
  • Numbers the text marks as official (call centre, hotline, resmi) or as the victim's (nomor milik korban) are skipped.
  • Account holder names are never stored, only the number (and the bank).
  • Phone numbers, bank accounts and e-wallets that no item has mentioned for a year are deleted by the nightly housekeeping (fraud_identifier_days; crypto wallets are not personal data and stay).
  • Identifiers never leave JATMP: they are left out of the REST API, the IOC feeds, STIX / TAXII, webhooks (also for watched identifiers) and MISP pushes.
  • Item text sent to a cloud AI model has phone numbers, bank accounts, e-wallets, e-mail addresses and long ID numbers replaced with placeholders first, whether or not they were extracted (setting Personal data in prompts, Settings → AI).
  • Extraction can be turned off entirely (Extract scammer phone numbers… under Settings → Scam & fraud).

Bank accounts link to cekrekening.id and wallets to a block explorer so an analyst can look them up by hand; JATMP does not query them (cekrekening.id sits behind a CAPTCHA).

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
Dashboard → Scams & fraud (/fraud) works like the cyber threats dashboard, with the same period switch (7 days to 1 year) and International / National view:

  • Scam reports over time, stacked by the five most reported scam types of the period, and a globe of the most targeted countries (provinces in the National view); click one for its scam reports.
  • Tiles with sparklines: scam reports against the period before, the largest reported loss (and victim count), scam types reported (and how many are spreading this week), brands impersonated and scammer identifiers.
  • Trending scam types (the period against the one before, with the malware and brands seen alongside and a spreading badge), most impersonated brands and the latest scammer identifiers.
  • Charts of reports by scam type, by kind of impersonated brand (banks, e-wallets, couriers, government…), by sector (critical infrastructure sectors) and per source.
  • Recent scam reports, the highest fraud scores and the fraud sources with their status.

docs.title: Pages
docs.text:
Scam reports are the second feed: Feed → Scams & fraud (/feed/scams, a tab next to Cyber threats on the Feed page). It lists every scam report, filterable by scam type, brand, sector, minimum fraud score, period and text (and by target country or province when opened from the globe), sortable by fraud score, loss, victims and time. The old address /fraud/items forwards there with its filters.

The other pages are in the menu's Intelligence dropdown, in its scams part:

  • Scam types and Brands & people (impersonated brands and people, with a Type filter): the usual entity tables (mentions, sources, trend, first / last seen) with the malware and brands or scam types seen alongside.
  • Scammer identifiers: phone numbers, bank accounts, e-wallets and wallets with the scam types and brands they appeared with, where they were seen, and a Copy button.

Scam types and brands also appear as chips in the feed, on item pages and in the relationship graph.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
Scam reports come from every source, and a few are added for this section (topic scam & fraud, see Sources): FBI IC3 public service announcements, CekFakta.com and Liputan6 Cek Fakta (filtered to scam reports), and ScamSniffer's crypto phishing blocklist. Any source can be given the topic scam & fraud under Settings → Sources → Edit; such sources show on the overview, and a single scam word is enough there to file an entry under Other scam.

Not included, after checking: OJK and Komdigi reject automated clients, turnbackhoax.id was down, OpenPhish forbids fetching its feed in robots.txt, PhishTank no longer registers new users, the FTC has no feed, Chainabuse needs a key, and Reddit's r/Scams is mostly victims' own posts (personal data).

docs.title: Re-running the analysis
docs.text: Existing items are analysed once in the background after an upgrade, and again whenever the rules change. To run it by hand: Re-analyse items on the dashboard or under Settings → Scam & fraud, or python manage.py fraudtag. Re-analysis loads items in chunks and only touches the database for items that are, or were, about a scam, so it runs in about the time it takes to read the items.

docs.title: When the analysis is wrong
docs.text: If an item isn't really about a scam, an analyst or admin can open the fraud-score popover on the item page and choose Not a scam report, with a reason. The fraud score drops to 0, the item's scam types, brands and identifiers are removed, and it leaves the scam section. The correction stays in force when the analysis is run again, and it can be undone on the Corrections page. A wrong brand or scam type on a real scam report can be removed with the ✕ next to it. See Corrections and quality.

docs.title: Processing
docs.text: Collection and analysis are built to stay cheap as the blocklists grow: the indicators of an item are looked up and created with one query per indicator type (a ScamSniffer day with hundreds of domains costs a handful of queries), blocklist verdicts are written in bulk instead of waiting for the enrichment providers, and the spread velocity of a scam type is counted once per type and day for a whole collection batch. Fact-check feeds are filtered to scam reports before anything is stored.

docs.title: Geography and Indonesia
docs.text: This page explains where each item's targets, reporting and infrastructure are located, how the International / National (Indonesia) view works, and how JATMP handles Bahasa Indonesia. The exact scoring rules are in Ingest and analysis.

docs.title: Three kinds of location
docs.text:
JATMP keeps three kinds of location apart, so that hosting countries never inflate the map of targets.

Target countries (and, for Indonesia, the province) are where the victims are or where the activity takes place. They come from:

  • place names and nationalities in the text;
  • the 38 Indonesian provinces with their cities and regencies (an ambiguous name such as Malang or Palu only counts after Kota, Kabupaten, Pemkot and the like);
  • Indonesian institutions and companies (BSSN, Komdigi, BPJS, OJK, Pertamina…);
  • .go.id, .co.id and .ac.id domains;
  • the victim country of leak-site postings, and the targeted countries that OTX and ransomware.live provide.

A country that describes the attacker is not a target: "Russian hackers", "China-nexus", "Iran-linked", "attributed to North Korea", "peretas asal Rusia". Nor is a marketplace or a hosting location: "sold on Russian forums", "hosted in the Netherlands", "a Dutch hosting provider". Cities outside Indonesia are not recognised, so "a Dubai-based exchange" names no country.

Source country is the outlet's country (set per source), or Indonesia for items written in Indonesian.

Hosting country of an IP indicator comes from an offline GeoIP database when one is installed (DB-IP Lite, or MaxMind GeoLite2 with a key). Otherwise it comes from the enrichment providers (IPinfo, VirusTotal, AbuseIPDB, OTX and others).

docs.title: Geography page
docs.text:
The Geography page shows target countries on a world map and Indonesian provinces on a province map, both linking to the matching feed. It also lists the families and actors named for each country, as well as hosting countries, source countries and languages. Target countries count stories, so a story carried by several outlets counts once; source countries and languages count each outlet's items.

The maps are drawn from public-domain Natural Earth outlines that ship with JATMP, so nothing is loaded from outside. The map and list cards are the same height, and the lists scroll, so every target country and province is listed.

Item pages and previews show the targets, source country and language. The feed and the REST API can filter by country, province, src_country and lang.

On the dashboard, a globe shows the top 10 target countries of the selected period (or provinces in the National view), built from the same outlines; see the dashboard.

docs.title: International / National (ID)
docs.text: The switch in the top bar limits the dashboard, every list, the statistics, the report builder and the IOC table to Indonesia. In the National view you see items that target Indonesia, plus items from Indonesian outlets that don't name another target country. Your choice is remembered for the session.

docs.title: Bahasa Indonesia
docs.text:
The language of each item is detected automatically.

  • Severity. The scoring rules know Indonesian terms (kebocoran data, diretas, peretasan, penipuan, phising, dieksploitasi, uang tebusan, judi online…) and count an English term and its Indonesian equivalent once. Awareness pieces (tips, cara, kenali) are scored down, just like English guides.
  • Extraction. The extractor understands the Indonesian word order for new families ("ransomware Brain Cipher", "trojan perbankan Mamont").
  • Indicators. Indonesian news and government domains are never treated as indicators.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: You can run JATMP from source with Python 3.11 or newer, or with Docker. It doesn't need an external database and loads nothing from a CDN, so it also runs on an isolated network. (Collecting sources does, of course, need Internet access.)

docs.title: Install from source
docs.text:
Create a virtual environment and activate it:

python -m venv .venv

.venv\Scripts\activate        # Linux/macOS: source .venv/bin/activate

Install the dependencies:

pip install -r requirements.txt

Run the installer. It asks whether you want single-user or multi-user mode, and for any API keys and AI settings:

python install.py

Then start JATMP and open http://127.0.0.1:8000:

python run.py

You can also skip the installer: on first launch, the web interface shows the same setup wizard. For an unattended install, pass everything on the command line, for example python install.py --mode multi --admin admin --password 'StrongPassw0rd'.

The web wizard doesn't ask for a login, because no users exist yet. Run the first install on 127.0.0.1 (the default) before you expose the port to a network. If you open the wizard from another machine, it asks for a one-time setup token, which you will find in the log and in data/setup-token.

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
Copy the example environment file and start the containers:

cp .env.example .env

docker compose up -d --build

The container exposes /healthz and has a built-in HEALTHCHECK.

To run a local AI model next to it, start the llm profile and pull a model:

docker compose --profile llm up -d

docker compose exec ollama ollama pull llama3.1

Then set the base URL to http://ollama:11434 under Settings → AI → Advanced.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Configuration explains API keys, options and the daily schedule.
  • Sources lists what JATMP collects out of the box.
  • How JATMP works explains what happens to the data once it arrives.

docs.title: History and storage
docs.text: This page covers backfilling past data, the retention tiers, full-text search, and the optional PostgreSQL database.

docs.title: Backfill
docs.text:
The live collectors only see what each source lists right now. To fill in the past, use Manage → Backfill (admin only). You can pick 7 days, 30 days, 90 days or 1 year, or set your own range.

Each source shows how far back it can go and how:

  • WordPress sites (which includes many security blogs) return every post in the range through their REST API.
  • Other RSS feeds are rebuilt from Internet Archive snapshots of the feed.
  • Bluesky, Mastodon, OTX and MISP page back through their own history.
  • ransomware.live country and group sources return their full victim lists.
  • ThreatFox reaches back 7 days.

Estimate shows how many items to expect from each source before you start (the figure is exact for WordPress sites). Start backfill and Stop are just below the page description; Stop only appears while a backfill is running. The backfill runs in the background, one source at a time, with the usual progress bar and a summary notification at the end. Stopping cancels the queued sources straight away and lets the current source finish the page it is working on.

docs.title: How backfilled items are treated
docs.text:
Backfilled items keep their original publication dates and are marked as history. That means:

  • They don't appear as trending in the last 7 days, or as newly seen. They do count when you pick a longer dashboard period (15 days to 1 year), which is what they are for.
  • Sources that can't be backfilled leave gaps in those longer periods, and the dashboards point this out.
  • Their indicators are only sent to the enrichment providers if they are from the last 14 days, unless you enable enrichment for backfilled items. That keeps the free quotas for live data.
  • They don't trigger webhooks, MISP pushes or AI summaries, and they don't affect source health.

The details are in Collection.

docs.title: Retention tiers
docs.text:
By default, items keep their full text for 180 days. After that, they keep their title, link, entities, severity and a short snippet, and the bulky provider data is removed. Deleting old items altogether is off by default. Both settings are under Settings → General. Separately, whenever a feed repeats the full text in its provider data, that copy is dropped as soon as the item is stored.

What exactly is kept, and when the nightly housekeeping runs, is described in Housekeeping and re-analysis.

docs.title: Search
docs.text: Search looks through the title and text of every item, matching the beginnings of words (so steal finds "stealer"). On SQLite it uses the FTS5 full-text index; on PostgreSQL it uses a full-text index of its own. Only a SQLite build without FTS5 falls back to plain substring matching. Whatever you type is never passed to the search engine as query syntax.

docs.title: PostgreSQL
docs.text: PostgreSQL is optional and useful for large installations. Start the bundled database with the postgres compose profile, or point JATMP_DATABASE_URL at your own server. To move an existing SQLite installation over, run python manage.py copy-db with the new database's URL.

docs.title: Sharing and integrations
docs.text: This page explains how other tools read data out of JATMP, how JATMP pushes data out, and the rules that decide what may leave. The rules themselves are described step by step in Sharing and delivery.

docs.title: REST API v1
docs.text:
The REST API lives under /api/v1/…, with a reference at /api/v1/docs that works offline. Its read-only endpoints cover items, entities, indicators and trends, with cursor pagination and since filters, so SIEMs, TIPs and scripts can poll for what is new.

To authenticate, create a personal API key under Profile → API keys and send it as Authorization: Bearer jatmp_…. Each key has scopes (read, export), an expiry date and its own rate limit, and can be revoked at any time. JATMP only stores a hash of the key. Browser sessions work too.

Items that are scam reports include a fraud object (score, loss_idr, victims, scam_types, brands, plus detail on single items). Indicators include verdict_at, the date their verdict was last given or confirmed. Scammer identifiers (phone numbers, bank accounts, e-wallets and crypto wallets) are never part of the API, the feeds, STIX / TAXII, webhooks or MISP pushes; see Scams and fraud.

docs.title: IOC export feeds
docs.text:
/api/v1/feeds/iocs.csv, .json and .txt export indicators. You can filter them by type, verdict (malicious by default), family, age, and a confidence from 0 to 100 that grows with the number of providers that agree. The .txt feed has one value per line, so it works as a firewall or proxy blocklist (a Palo Alto EDL or a FortiGate threat feed, for example).

IPs, domains and URLs whose malicious verdict hasn't been confirmed for 60 days are left out of the feeds, so a blocklist built from them doesn't keep blocking addresses that have changed hands. See Verdicts that age.

docs.title: STIX 2.1 and TAXII 2.1
docs.text:
/api/v1/stix/bundle, /stix/items/<id> and /stix/entities/<id> export reports, malware, intrusion sets, vulnerabilities, attack patterns and indicators (with STIX patterns, indicates relationships and TLP markings). The ⇩ STIX button on item and entity pages downloads the same thing. IP, domain and URL indicators carry a valid_until date based on when their verdict was last confirmed.

A read-only TAXII 2.1 server at /taxii2/ offers two collections, indicators and reports, with added_after, pagination and match[type], so OpenCTI, MISP, Sentinel or Splunk can subscribe. TAXII clients authenticate with an API key, either as a Bearer token or as the HTTP Basic password. Object ids stay the same for each installation, so consumers update objects rather than duplicating them.

docs.title: Webhooks
docs.text:
Webhooks are set up under Settings → Webhooks. You can subscribe to four events: a new high-severity item, a watched entity being mentioned, an indicator turning malicious, and a job failing.

Generic receivers get signed JSON (X-JATMP-Signature: sha256=HMAC(secret, "<timestamp>.<body>")), while Slack, Discord and Teams get ready-made messages. Failed deliveries are retried with increasing delays, and every delivery is listed with its status.

docs.title: MISP, both ways
docs.text:
From MISP: a MISP events source pulls events in. Attributes become indicators, galaxy clusters become actors and families, and the event's TLP is kept.

To MISP: Send to MISP on item, family and actor pages creates an event with TLP and family tags and the indicators as attributes. New items above a severity threshold can also be pushed automatically. Events that came from MISP are never pushed back.

docs.title: Sharing rules
docs.text:
Everything above goes through the same set of rules:

  • TLP. Every item has a TLP: its own (from OTX or MISP), or its source's, or CLEAR if neither is set. Only items up to the configured maximum (TLP:GREEN by default) leave JATMP. When you add a source, the form asks for its TLP and tells you whether its items will be shared.
  • Redistribution. Sources can be marked "not shared". ANY.RUN and ransomware.live are not shared by default, because of their terms.
  • Provider details stay inside JATMP unless an admin enables them. JATMP's own verdict is always shared.

docs.title: Dark web (tier 1)
docs.text:
JATMP only uses clearnet aggregators. It never visits leak sites or forums, never logs in anywhere, never solves CAPTCHAs, and never downloads leaked data.

Deep dive on a ransomware family or actor page asks ransomware.live for the group's leak-site victims (count, countries, sectors, recent victims, the CVEs it exploits, and its tools) and links the CVEs. On a domain page, it asks Hudson Rock how many employees and users of that domain were infected by infostealers (counts only, never credentials).

ransomware.live's keyless API is for personal use only, so organisations should add the free PRO key. That is why the ransomware.live sources start out disabled.

docs.title: Maintenance commands
docs.text:
manage.py runs jobs and maintenance tasks from the command line. Many of them also have a button in the interface, noted below. Most of these jobs also run on their own schedule; see A day on the scheduler.

python manage.py collect          # run every collector now (or only some: collect 1 5 7)
python manage.py enrich           # run one enrichment batch
python manage.py cve-intel        # refresh CISA KEV, EPSS and CVSS for recently mentioned CVEs
python manage.py digest           # write the AI executive summary now
python manage.py reextract        # extract the entities of every item again
python manage.py ioc-clean        # dry run: IP / SHA-1 indicators the extractor now rejects; add --apply to remove them
python manage.py rescore          # recalculate severity with the current rules (also a button in Settings → General)
python manage.py seed-sources     # add new built-in sources to an existing install (also a button in Settings)
python manage.py slim             # apply the retention tier now (trim the text of old items)
python manage.py geotag           # re-run the geography (targets, provinces, language, source country)
python manage.py geoip-update     # download the offline GeoIP database and locate IP indicators
python manage.py fraudtag         # re-run the scam & fraud analysis on every item (also a button on the fraud pages)
python manage.py sectortag        # detect the critical infrastructure sectors of every item again
python manage.py digesttag        # flag the newsletters and round-ups again (after changing a source's "digest" setting)
python manage.py quality          # precision and recall of the detection rules on the cases in tests/quality/
python manage.py telegram-login   # sign in to Telegram once for MTProto (optional; needs requirements-telegram.txt)
python manage.py vacuum           # give freed disk space back after deleting a lot of data
python manage.py copy-db postgresql+psycopg://jatmp:secret@localhost:5432/jatmp   # copy everything into an empty database
python manage.py create-user alice analyst

Re-scoring and re-extraction keep the points that don't come from the text (the enrichment bonus and the last AI assessment), so they never drop a confirmed item below a threshold. They also keep analysts' corrections: a link an analyst removed is not added back. After an upgrade that changes the scoring, fraud, sector or geography rules, the matching re-analysis runs on its own; changes to entity extraction need reextract, and the upgrade notes say when. See Housekeeping and re-analysis.

docs.title: The quality report
docs.text:
python manage.py quality runs the detection rules over the labelled cases in tests/quality/ and prints the precision, recall and F1 of each area (families and actors, indicators, scam reports, sectors, target countries, severity), followed by the cases the rules got wrong. Options:

Option What it does --corrections FILE Adds an export of the analysts' corrections (Export as test cases on the Corrections page) and reports how many of them the current rules would still repeat --summary Prints the numbers without the list of wrong cases --json Prints the result as JSON --check Exits with an error when an area falls below tests/quality/baseline.json (what CI does) --update-baseline Records the current numbers as the new baseline (only without --corrections)

What the areas measure and how to read the numbers is explained in Corrections and quality.

docs.title: Reporting and AI
docs.text: This page covers the Threat Intel Findings report builder and the optional AI features. How the AI features work in detail, and what they send to a model, is explained in AI processing.

docs.title: Reporting
docs.text:
The report builder produces a Threat Intel Findings document for any period, as PDF, Word, Markdown or CSV.

The report opens with a summary of the period and then writes up the top findings: when each was published, its severity, a description, the related malware, actors and CVEs, and a link to the original. It then lists the leading malware families, with their type, the sources that covered them and an example hash, and closes with the top indicators of compromise and their verdicts.

You can also add collection statistics, actors, CVEs, newly seen families and the latest AI executive summary, and you can choose how many findings, families and indicators to include. Like the dashboards, the report counts a story carried by several outlets once.

docs.title: AI (optional)
docs.text:
With an AI model configured, JATMP can:

  • summarise and analyse individual items;
  • write a threat brief about a family, actor or other entity;
  • write a daily executive summary;
  • answer questions about the collected data.

docs.title: Setting it up
docs.text:
Setting up the AI is a three-way choice between Off, Local and Cloud. You then pick a vendor, and a model from the live list that the server or provider reports:

  • Local runtimes: Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM, Jan, or any OpenAI-compatible server.
  • Cloud providers: Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq, Gemini, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, Together, or any OpenAI-compatible API.

You can also choose the language the AI writes in. The model names in the presets were current when this version was released; use Load models to see what your server or provider actually offers.

docs.title: Personal data
docs.text: Item text can contain phone numbers, bank accounts and e-mail addresses. With a cloud model, JATMP replaces them with placeholders ([phone 1], [account 1] and so on) before a prompt is sent, so they never reach the provider. The setting Personal data in prompts (Settings → AI) controls this: cloud (the default) redacts for cloud models only, always redacts for every model, and never switches it off. See What leaves your network.

docs.title: The executive summary
docs.text:
The executive summary appears on the dashboard card and behind the AI summary button, and older ones are kept under AI insights. It is short on purpose: a one-sentence headline, an overall threat level (low, elevated, high or critical), three or four key points, and up to three actions for today. It is based on the last 24 hours of items plus the week's trending malware, actors, CVEs, scam types and sectors.

The model answers in JSON. JATMP checks the answer, removes any Markdown or maths notation, and displays it with the same components as the rest of the interface. If the answer can't be used, the text is shown as it came.

The summary runs every day at 06:00 UTC by default. You can change the time and the time zone under Settings → General; see Daily schedule.

docs.title: Asking questions
docs.text:
Ask on the AI insights page answers a question from the data JATMP has collected. Before the model sees the question, JATMP picks the items that fit it best: the families, actors, CVEs and indicators the question names (aliases included, so "Fancy Bear" finds APT28), the malware types and sectors it mentions ("ransomware on hospitals" finds "LockBit hits a healthcare provider"), the period it names ("this week", "minggu ini"), and its words through the full-text index. A syndicated story counts once.

The answer cites the items it is based on as [1], [2] and so on, each linking to the item, and lists below it which items were used and why they matched. The model is told to answer only from those items and to say when something is missing. See Questions.
