docs.text:
A tour of the current interface, taken on a test install filled from public sources (no enrichment keys, so most indicators show as pending).

Cyber threats dashboard: the collapsible sidebar (Cyber threats, Scams & fraud and Feed on top, then the Intelligence, Analysis and Manage dropdowns, shown here with Intelligence open; the arrow by the logo folds the whole menu into an icon rail), the period switch (7 days to 1 year) with the backfill note, International / National (ID) switch, Collect now / Enrich now with last and next run, headline ticker, threat radar with families, CVEs and actors, the globe of the top 10 target countries, and the KPI tiles.

Trending malware, CVEs (CISA KEV, CVSS, EPSS, risk-weighted priority) and threat actors over the chosen period Top 5 trending over time next to the critical infrastructure sectors of the period

Scams & fraud dashboard (0.10): scam reports over time stacked by scam type, the most targeted countries, tiles for reports, losses, scam types, brands and scammer identifiers, then trending scam types, impersonated brands and the latest identifiers.

Scam reports ranked by fraud score, with losses in rupiah, scam types and brands Feed with the side preview: severity breakdown, entities and indicators without leaving the list Item page: severity, STIX export, extracted entities with their verdicts Relationship graph: the item, its entities and the other items that share them Geography: target countries on a world map, with the families and actors named per country National (ID) view: the dashboard limited to Indonesia, with the globe on the provinces Malware family page: timeline, coverage per source, Deep dive, graph, co-mentioned entities IOC table with verdicts, hosting countries, attributed families and where each indicator was seen Malware families: unified table with trend score, related entities and pagination CVE list sorted by EPSS, with KEV badges, co-mentioned families and the New threats button Historical backfill: Start backfill under the description, per-source reach and method, estimates and storage statistics AI settings: local or cloud, vendor presets and a live model list Report builder: period, content and format for the Threat Intel Findings document

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Content-Security-Policy. Scripts load only from the application's origin plus a per-request nonce for the few inline blocks; there are no inline event handlers, and Chart.js is vendored under app/static/js/vendor. X-Frame-Options: DENY, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, COOP and Cache-Control: no-store are set on every page.
  • Untrusted feed content. HTML is stripped and entities are decoded on ingest. Item URLs are kept only when they use http(s), so a feed cannot smuggle a javascript: link into the UI. Markdown returned by the LLM is rendered with raw HTML disabled. The text cleaners avoid nested quantifiers and are tested against hostile input, so one crafted article cannot hang a collector thread (regular-expression denial of service).
  • Outbound requests. Feeds, intel providers, the AI, MISP and the GeoIP download only reach public addresses. The check runs on every redirect hop, and the connection goes to the address that was checked, so a DNS rebinding name cannot swap in 127.0.0.1 afterwards. Private hosts that JATMP should reach (an internal MISP, a self-hosted RSS-Bridge) are listed under Settings → Sharing & API → Private hosts JATMP may contact; a local AI server is added there when you save the AI tab in local mode. Response bodies are capped after decompression (20 MB by default), so a huge feed or a gzip bomb is refused instead of filling the memory.
  • AI output is advisory. Article text is attacker-controlled, and so is whatever a model reads out of it. The AI summary may raise an item's severity by at most 20 points, listed as AI assessment in the breakdown; it may link known families and actors, but a new family only when another source already reported it; AI-proposed entities and tags carry an AI badge.
  • Exports. CSV reports and the CSV IOC feed prefix text cells that start with =, +, - or @ with an apostrophe, so a feed title cannot run as a spreadsheet formula.
  • Manual lookups. Enrichment, context lookups, deep dives and AI summaries started from the UI are limited per user and minute and run once per entity at a time; Run now on a source does nothing while that source runs.
  • Sessions and authentication. Signed cookie sessions (SameSite=Lax, HttpOnly), CSRF synchroniser tokens on every POST, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with 600k iterations (older hashes are upgraded on login), a 15-minute lockout after five failed logins per username and IP, open-redirect-safe next handling and a session reset on login. Changing a password (or Sign out other sessions on the profile page) ends every other session of that user; an admin resetting a password ends that user's sessions.
  • First-run setup. Before installation the wizard is open, and whoever finishes it becomes the admin. From the machine itself that needs nothing; from any other address (another host, a Docker port mapping) the wizard also asks for a one-time setup token, printed in the log at start-up and stored in data/setup-token until the install is done.
  • Settings hygiene. Secret values are never sent back to the browser (only "configured" or "not set"), numeric settings are clamped so the VirusTotal throttle cannot be disabled by accident, and source URLs must be http(s).
  • Outbound API. API keys are 256-bit random secrets of which only a SHA-256 is stored; they carry scopes, expire, can be revoked by their owner or an admin, and are rate limited per key. Key creation, revocation and feed downloads are written to the audit log. Bearer requests need no CSRF token; every cookie-authenticated POST still does.
  • Corrections. Only analysts and admins can correct entities, verdicts and scam reports, or undo a correction; viewers can see them. Every correction needs a reason, is stored with its author, and is written to the audit log (correction_unlink, correction_verdict…, correction_undone), so a changed verdict can always be traced to a person.
  • Webhooks. Targets must resolve to public addresses (checked when saved and again before each delivery; redirects are not followed) unless an admin allows private ones. Signing secrets are derived from the session secret and a per-hook salt, so the database holds nothing that could forge a signature.
  • GeoIP download. The offline GeoIP database is fetched from download.db-ip.com (or download.maxmind.com with a license key) only when an admin asks for it or the monthly refresh is switched on; a download that is not a valid database is discarded. IP lookups themselves never leave the host.
  • Sharing. TLP and per-source redistribution flags gate the API, exports, webhooks and MISP pushes (see Sharing and integrations).
  • API keys entered in the UI (provider keys, the AI key, the Telegram session) are stored encrypted in the local database (Fernet, with a key derived from the secret in data/config.json). A copy of the database alone does not reveal them; back up data/config.json together with the database, or the keys have to be entered again. On shared hosts prefer environment variables, which lock the corresponding fields. data/config.json holds the session secret and is written with mode 0600.
  • Dependencies. requirements.lock pins every package; Docker and CI install with it, CI runs pip-audit against it, and Dependabot proposes updates weekly.
  • /healthz (unauthenticated) reports liveness only, not the version.
  • When exposing the platform beyond localhost, run it behind a TLS-terminating reverse proxy and set JATMP_SECURE_COOKIES=1.

docs.title: Personal data in scam reports
docs.text:
Scam reports can contain phone numbers and bank accounts. JATMP takes them only from scam reports and only where the text marks them as the scammer's, skips official and victims' numbers, never stores account holder names, deletes them after a year without mentions, and never shares them through the API, feeds, STIX / TAXII, webhooks or MISP. Details in Scams and fraud.

Prompts to a cloud AI model have phone numbers, bank accounts, e-wallets, e-mail addresses and long ID numbers replaced with placeholders first (Personal data in prompts under Settings → AI); see AI processing.

docs.title: Telegram session
docs.text: The optional MTProto session string (telegram_session) gives full access to the Telegram account it was created with. It is stored like the other secrets (never shown in the UI, never logged); prefer TELEGRAM_SESSION in the environment on shared hosts, use a separate account, and end the session from Telegram's Active sessions list if the database leaks. The web-preview mode needs no account at all.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
What JATMP collects out of the box. Every source can be edited, disabled or removed under Settings → Sources, and any RSS / Atom feed, Bluesky or Mastodon account, X account, public Telegram channel or threat-intel query can be added there.

Sources that a newer version adds to the built-in list join an existing install automatically when it starts, and a notification lists them. JATMP remembers which built-in sources it has already offered, so one you deleted does not come back. Add new built-in sources (or python manage.py seed-sources) adds every missing built-in source, deleted ones included.

BSSN, Kompas and Tempo are not included: their sites refuse automated clients or forbid automated collection. API keys for the threat-intel collectors and X are set under Settings → Threat-intel APIs or through environment variables; see Configuration. How far back each source can be crawled is shown on the backfill page; see History and storage.

docs.title: Topic filters
docs.text:
Any news or social source (RSS, Telegram, X, Mastodon, Bluesky) can carry a topic filter (Filter in the source's Edit dialog), for example to keep only the cyber posts of a general news channel:

  • security keeps only entries about breaches, hacking, fraud, malware and the like (English and Indonesian terms). Used for the general technology sections of Indonesian outlets.
  • cyber is the stricter version for general news sections (national, economy, law). Words that are fine in a tech section mean something else there ("tabung gas bocor", "modus penyelundupan", a hijacked bus), so only unambiguous cyber and digital-fraud terms count (serangan siber, data … bocor, situs diretas, judi online, penipuan online, anti-scam…), plus anything the fraud rules recognise as a scam report.
  • fraud keeps only entries about a scam (the scam-type rules of the fraud analysis). Used for fact-checkers, whose feeds are mostly political hoaxes.

Separately, a source can have the topic scam & fraud (also in the Edit dialog). It then shows on the fraud overview, and a single scam word is enough to file one of its entries under Other scam.

docs.title: Telegram
docs.text:
Add a source of kind Telegram public channel with the channel's username or t.me link. By default JATMP reads the channel's public web preview (https://t.me/s/<channel>), which needs no account: 20 posts per page, older pages for a backfill (up to 3,000 posts per run). Posts keep their links, forwarded-from name, attached file names and view count; posts without text (a bare photo or sticker) are skipped.

Channels that turned the web preview off, or a deeper backfill, need MTProto:

  1. pip install -r requirements-telegram.txt (Telethon).
  2. Create an application at my.telegram.org and enter its api_id and api_hash under Settings → Social (or TELEGRAM_API_ID / TELEGRAM_API_HASH).
  3. Run python manage.py telegram-login once. It asks for the phone number, the login code and the two-step password if set, and stores the session string (telegram_session).

From then on Telegram sources use MTProto automatically; set Via to web or mtproto on a source to force one. Both ways produce the same item ids, so switching never duplicates posts. Only public channels are read: JATMP does not join channels, read private groups or post. Use a separate Telegram account, because the session string gives full access to it.

Channels run by threat actors (hacktivist groups, leak and fraud markets) are not built in: they are renamed or banned often, and following one is an analyst's decision. Add them like any other channel.

docs.title: Scam and fraud sources
docs.text:
Source What it adds FBI IC3 public service announcements US fraud warnings (election, investment, impersonation scams) CekFakta.com, Liputan6 Cek Fakta Indonesian fact-checks about scams (fake bank accounts, bansos links, job offers), filtered with the fraud topic filter ScamSniffer crypto phishing domains One item per day of newly listed wallet-drainer and fake-airdrop domains (GPL-3.0 list, published a week late). The domains are marked malicious on arrival, so they do not use enrichment quota. Backfill reaches back to May 2022

Scam reports also come from the news, social and Telegram sources. See Scams and fraud.

docs.title: Account verification
docs.text: The Bluesky and Mastodon accounts listed above were verified active on 12 November 2026, with three exceptions: vxunderground.bsky.social has no posts yet, and Marcus Hutchins and MalwareHunterTeam rarely post on Bluesky (their main activity is on X; Marcus Hutchins is also on Mastodon). X handles cannot be verified without an API token. The Telegram channels and the scam & fraud sources were verified on 16 November 2026.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text: Schema changes are applied automatically on start-up (new tables and columns; there are no manual migrations). The notes below list what else to do when moving to a version. After any upgrade, run pip install -r requirements.txt (or rebuild the Docker image) and restart. The full list of changes is in the changelog.

docs.title: Upgrading to the next release (unreleased)
docs.text:
One new column and a clean-up command. No manual migration.

  • Newsletters are flagged on their own. The new column items.is_digest is added at start-up, and about 75 seconds later run_digesttag flags the newsletters and round-ups among the stored items once (its progress is in the job status). Correlation and co-mentions use the flag from then on.
  • Remove the false IP and SHA-1 indicators that version numbers and git commits created. Run the dry run first, check the numbers, then apply:
python manage.py ioc-clean
python manage.py ioc-clean --apply

It only removes regex links of IP and SHA-1 indicators that the current extractor rejects, and only where the item's text is still stored. Prefer it to reextract, which rebuilds everything from the stored text and so cannot find again what retention has trimmed. - Scam reports are re-analysed once (fraud rules version 7) in the background after start-up: brands that only speak or act lose their impersonated link, items about anti-scam tools leave the scam section, and impersonated people (brand type person) are added. Brands and scam types removed by an analyst stay removed. Bookmarks of /fraud/items keep working; the page is now /feed/scams. - Optional: to force a source to count as a newsletter (or never to), set "digest": true or false in its stored config and run python manage.py digesttag.

docs.title: Upgrading to 0.14.0
docs.text:
Navigation changes and higher minimum versions. No schema change, no re-analysis.

  • Run pip install -r requirements.txt again (and requirements-postgres.txt or requirements-telegram.txt if you use them): anthropic 2.8.0, feedparser 6.0.14, python-docx 1.2.0, psycopg 3.3.9 and telethon 1.45.0 are now the minimums. The Docker image installs from the lock file as before.
  • Feed filters now stay for the session. A link or form that names one filter changes only that one; Clear filters drops them all. Bookmarks keep working, but opening the Feed from the menu shows your last filters.
  • The menu is regrouped: Intelligence, Analysis and Manage are dropdowns, and the whole menu folds into an icon rail. Nothing to configure; the state is kept in the browser.

docs.title: Upgrading to 0.13.1
docs.text:
Rule tuning from the first quality report. No new dependency, no schema change.

  • One-off re-analysis at start-up, as after other rule changes: geography (GEO_VERSION 2), scam analysis (fraud.RULES_VERSION 6), sectors (sectors.RULES_VERSION 3) and severity (severity.RULES_VERSION 2) of every stored item. Expect some target countries to disappear (marketplaces, hosting), more items recognised as scam reports, and some serious incidents to rise into the notable list.
  • Entity extraction is not re-run automatically. Run python manage.py reextract to apply the new indicator rules (public resolvers, paste and file-sharing services, "server 1.2.3.4") and the family names written in their own spelling ("RedLine", "Cl0p") to stored items. It keeps analysts' corrections, enrichment bonuses and AI assessments.

docs.title: Upgrading to 0.13.0
docs.text:
Analyst corrections, quality measurement, topic filters for every source kind and better Q&A. No new dependency. One new table (corrections) is created on start-up.

  • Corrections. Analysts and admins see ✕ next to entities on item pages, ✎ Correct on entity pages and Not a scam report on scam items; viewers see the corrections but can't make them. Nothing changes until someone corrects something. See Corrections and quality.
  • Topic filters on social sources. Telegram, X, Mastodon and Bluesky sources now have a Filter field. Existing sources keep taking everything until you set one; for a general news channel, cyber is the usual choice.
  • Q&A finds items by the entities, malware types and sectors a question names, and its answers link the items they cite. Old answers are unchanged.
  • CI runs the quality gate (tests/test_quality.py). If you maintain your own rule changes, run python manage.py quality before pushing.
  • A repair at start-up: articles marked as a copy of themselves (possible since the 0.10.1 upgrade) become originals again and reappear in the feed; the log says how many ("repaired N item(s)").

docs.title: Upgrading to 0.12.0
docs.text:
Trust and coverage items from the product review. No new dependency. One new column (entities.verdict_at) is created on start-up.

  • Counts change. Every dashboard figure now counts a story that several outlets carry once: Items collected became Stories collected and is lower than before, and so are the timelines, breakdowns, map counts, entity mentions and the PDF / Word report totals. Items per source still counts every copy.
  • One re-score after the upgrade. About 90 seconds after the first start, every stored item is re-scored with the current severity rules (a background job, no network; it keeps enrichment bonuses and AI assessments) and a notification says when it is done. On a large install it takes a few minutes.
  • Verdicts age. Malicious and suspicious IPs, domains and URLs are looked up again after 30 days (verdict_recheck_days) and may come back lower; they leave the IOC export feeds and TAXII once their verdict is older than 60 days and was not confirmed again (verdict_feed_days). Both are under Settings → Enrichment; 0 turns them off. Expect your blocklist feed to shrink over the first weeks, and a few more lookups per run.
  • Personal data is redacted from prompts to a cloud AI model by default. Set Personal data in prompts to Never redact under Settings → AI to keep the old behaviour.
  • Source health notifications: expect a notification for sources that have been quiet for three times their usual gap or failing for a day; the Sources tab lists them.

docs.title: Upgrading to 0.11.0
docs.text:
Quick wins from a product review. New dependency tzdata (time zones on slim images and Windows): run pip install -r requirements.txt -c requirements.lock, or rebuild the Docker image. No schema changes.

  • Daily schedule. The executive summary (06:00) and housekeeping (03:30) still run in UTC until you set a time zone and times under Settings → General (or JATMP_TIMEZONE). A team in Jakarta usually wants Asia/Jakarta and 07:00; see Configuration.
  • The feed hides syndicated copies by default and says how many it left out; Show copies lists them again. Bookmarked feed links show fewer rows than before for stories carried by several outlets.
  • Re-scoring keeps points. Re-score all items and manage.py reextract now keep the enrichment bonus and the last AI assessment. Items re-scored by an older version lost their AI points; Analyse with AI again on the ones that matter. After an older reextract, one Re-score all items restores the enrichment bonus (the verdicts are stored on the indicators).
  • ThreatFox items are keyed by the day ThreatFox first saw the IOCs and take in IOCs reported later that day. Items stored before the upgrade are not changed.
  • New sources ask for a TLP. Existing sources without a TLP keep counting as CLEAR (shared); Settings → Sharing & API says how many there are.
  • Quota warnings now come for every provider with a daily budget (GreyNoise, AbuseIPDB, context providers), not only VirusTotal: expect a notification on days a small budget such as GreyNoise's 40 runs out.

docs.title: Upgrading to 0.10.1
docs.text:
Fixes from a security, data-processing and efficiency audit. Install the new dependency (cryptography) with pip install -r requirements.txt -c requirements.lock, or rebuild the Docker image.

  • API keys are encrypted in the database on the first start. Keep data/config.json with your database backups from now on: without it the stored keys cannot be read and must be entered again.
  • Outbound guard. Feeds, providers, the AI and MISP may only reach public addresses. Private hosts you already configured (a local Ollama, an internal MISP, an RSS-Bridge on the LAN, a feed on a .local name) are added to Settings → Sharing & API → Private hosts JATMP may contact on the first start. Anything private you add later goes there by hand (a local AI server is added for you when you save the AI tab in local mode); a blocked request says so in the source's error.
  • First-run setup from another machine (or through Docker's port mapping) asks for a setup token. It is in the log (docker compose logs jatmp) and in data/setup-token.
  • New columns (users.session_version, items.fingerprint, items.dup_of) and indexes on items and entities are created on start-up.
  • One-off start-up jobs, without network requests: syndicated copies of the same story from different outlets are marked (statistics, trending and the executive summary count them once); the scam & fraud analysis and the sector tags are recomputed with the new rules.
  • Malware families, actors and severity use stricter rules (everyday words such as Bitter or Pegasus need a qualifier, demonyms and platform names are no new family, a guessed family no longer outscores a known one, "critical infrastructure" is no critical bug). Stored items keep their old entities until you run python manage.py reextract, which also recomputes severities.
  • /healthz no longer reports the version.

docs.title: Upgrading to 0.10
docs.text:
• New column insights.data (the structured executive summary) is created on start-up.
  • About a minute after the first start, a background job tags every existing item with its critical infrastructure sectors (no network requests; python manage.py sectortag does the same).
  • The scam & fraud rules changed (vendor listicles, criminal-charge names), so the start-up job re-analyses stored items once, as after 0.9.
  • A one-off start-up job removes stylesheet text that some feeds printed into stored items (no network requests).
  • The dashboard at / is now Cyber threats; the scam & fraud overview at /fraud became a dashboard of its own, and the scam pages moved from tabs into the sidebar. Bookmarks keep working.
  • The daily AI digest is now a short executive summary. Nothing to configure; the next scheduled or manual run writes the new format.

docs.title: Upgrading to 0.9.1
docs.text: • New built-in sources are added automatically on start-up from now on (a notification lists them). The first start after this upgrade adds every built-in source the install does not have, the 15 Indonesian news sections included; a built-in source you deleted earlier comes back once in that run, so delete it again if needed. After that, deleted built-in sources stay deleted.

docs.title: Upgrading to 0.9
docs.text:
• New columns sources.topic, items.fraud_score, items.fraud_detail, items.fraud_loss_idr and items.fraud_victims are created on start-up.
  • About 40 seconds after the first start, a background job runs the scam & fraud analysis on every existing item (Re-analyse items under Settings → Scam & fraud does the same, and so does python manage.py fraudtag). No network requests.
  • Add new built-in sources under Settings → Sources adds the Telegram channels (vx-underground enabled, three disabled), FBI IC3, CekFakta.com, Liputan6 Cek Fakta and ScamSniffer.
  • Telegram needs nothing more for public channels. For MTProto, pip install -r requirements-telegram.txt and run python manage.py telegram-login (optional; see Sources).
  • manage.py reextract now also rebuilds the scam types, brands and identifiers.
  • Scammer phone numbers, bank accounts and e-wallets not mentioned for 365 days are deleted by the nightly housekeeping; change or turn this off under Settings → Scam & fraud.

docs.title: Upgrading to 0.8
docs.text:
• New table item_geo and columns items.lang, items.src_country, sources.country, sources.language and entities.country are created on start-up. Columns added this way now get their default value on existing rows (earlier versions left them NULL).
  • About 20 seconds after the first start, a background job assigns target countries, provinces, language and source country to every existing item (Re-run geography under Settings → General does the same, and so does python manage.py geotag). No network requests.
  • Add new built-in sources under Settings → Sources adds the Indonesian news feeds (and, from 0.8.1, Seraphim News and two Indonesian X accounts). Set the country of your own outlets under Edit so they count for the source-country view (Indonesian ones also for the National view).
  • For hosting countries without provider lookups, press Download GeoIP database (Settings → General or the Geography page) or run python manage.py geoip-update.
  • Run python manage.py rescore to apply the Indonesian severity terms to items collected before the upgrade.
  • New dependency: maxminddb (pure Python), so run pip install -r requirements.txt again.
  • 0.8.2 changes no schema. Actors you added in data/knowledge_extra.json count as unclassified on the dashboard until you give them a category (see Configuration).

docs.title: Upgrading to 0.7
docs.text:
• New columns items.origin and items.slimmed_at are added on start-up, and the full-text index is built once (a few seconds per 100,000 items).
  • Retention changed. The default for deleting old items is now never (it was 180 days), because a backfill of a year would otherwise be deleted the same night; instead, items older than 180 days are slimmed to title, link, entities, severity and a snippet. An install where you saved a retention value keeps it, and the backfill does not reach further back than that.
  • PostgreSQL, Docker: in .env set JATMP_WITH_POSTGRES=1, JATMP_DB_PASSWORD=<strong password> and JATMP_DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://jatmp:<password>@db:5432/jatmp, then docker compose --profile postgres up -d --build. Without Docker: pip install -r requirements-postgres.txt. To bring existing data along, run python manage.py copy-db <url> against the new, empty database before switching JATMP_DATABASE_URL.

docs.title: Upgrading to 0.6
docs.text: No schema changes. Context providers are off until a key is set (or keyless lookups are allowed), and context lookups only run when someone presses Context lookup unless the automatic option is enabled. TAXII clients need an API key with the read scope; STIX downloads through the API need export.

docs.title: Upgrading to 0.5
docs.text: Automatic on start-up: new tables (api_keys, webhooks, webhook_deliveries) and columns (sources.tlp, sources.redistribute, items.tlp). Run Add new built-in sources under Settings → Sources to get the two ransomware.live sources (disabled). Existing items have no TLP of their own and count as their source's TLP (CLEAR unless you set one). In single-user mode the API, like the rest of the app, needs no login; keep such an install on localhost or use multi-user mode before exposing it.

docs.title: Upgrading to 0.4
docs.text: Nothing to do by hand: on start-up the new notifications table is created and the new columns on collector_runs and users are added. The first CVE lookup runs three minutes after start-up and fills in KEV / EPSS / CVSS for CVEs mentioned in the last 30 days; press Refresh CVE intel on the CVE page or run python manage.py cve-intel to start it right away.

docs.title: Upgrading to 0.3
docs.text: Severity scores and their breakdowns are computed when an item is ingested. Items collected by an earlier version keep their old score until you run python manage.py rescore or press Re-score all items under Settings → General; this is a local pass over the database and makes no network requests. The new severity_detail column is added automatically on start-up. Word and PDF export need two additional packages, so run pip install -r requirements.txt again.

docs.title: Using JATMP
docs.text: This page is a tour of the interface: install modes and roles, the dashboards, the tables and side preview, job status, and notifications.

docs.title: Install modes and roles
docs.text:
JATMP installs in one of two modes:

  • Single-user: no login, one built-in user.
  • Multi-user: logins with three roles (admin, analyst and viewer), user management, job status and an audit log.

In both modes, users keep a personal watchlist, and the interface has a dark and a light theme, a / shortcut for search, and a layout that works on a phone. The Docker image comes with a health check.

docs.title: Dashboards
docs.text:
The menu on the left starts with the two dashboards, Cyber threats (/) and Scams & fraud (/fraud, see Scams and fraud), followed by the Feed, which has the same two sides: Cyber threats (/feed, every item) and Scams & fraud (/feed/scams, the scam reports). Both are in the Feed dropdown and as tabs on the Feed page. Everything else is grouped in three dropdowns:

Group Pages Intelligence Malware, Threat actors, CVEs and IOCs for cyber threats; Scam types, Brands & people (impersonated brands and people) and Scammer identifiers for scams Analysis Geography, Watchlist, Reports, Corrections, AI insights Manage Settings, Backfill, and Admin in multi-user mode

A group opens by itself when the page you are on belongs to it, and otherwise remembers whether you left it open or closed. On a wider screen, the arrow next to the logo collapses the whole menu to a narrow rail of icons: hover over an icon to see its name, or click a group's icon to expand the menu with that group open. Both choices are remembered in your browser.

docs.title: Period
docs.text:
Both dashboards show the last 7 days by default. The switch under the title lets you pick 15 days, 30 days, 3 months, 6 months or 1 year, and everything on the page follows it: tiles, tables, charts, the radar and the globe. Your choice is remembered for the session, and charts switch to weekly bars for periods over 90 days.

The live collectors only see what sources list right now, so older days only contain what was backfilled. For periods longer than 7 days (or reaching back before you installed JATMP), the dashboard tells you so, shows how many backfilled items the period contains, and links admins to the Backfill page, where each source shows how far back it can go (History and storage).

docs.title: What's on the cyber threats dashboard
docs.text:
From top to bottom:

  • Threat radar and globe. The radar shows trending malware families (bug icon), CVEs (broken shield) and threat actors (hooded figure). The closer an entry is to the centre, the higher its trend score; the larger it is, the more it was mentioned. A dashed ring marks entries first seen in the period, and the buttons in the card header hide or show each type. The globe shows the top 10 target countries of the period (Indonesian provinces in the National view). It turns from one to the next, showing each one's count and the families and actors named there. Drag it to turn it, hover over a country to see its count, click one to open its feed, or use the numbered buttons, + / − and ⟲. Pointing at the globe pauses the tour; ▶ / ❚❚ starts or stops it.
  • KPI tiles. Stories collected, IOCs seen, active malware families, threat actors and CVEs discussed in the period, each compared with the period before and with a sparkline. A story that several outlets carry counts once; the Stories collected tile also shows the item count including copies.
  • Executive summary, if an AI model is configured (Reporting and AI).
  • Collection volume per day (or week) and source type.
  • Trending malware, Trending CVEs and Trending threat actors, each scrolling on its own. Hover over the CVSS, EPSS and priority column headers to see what they mean.
  • Top 5 trending over time, with a dropdown for families, CVEs or actors, next to Critical infrastructure sectors, which shows stories per sector (Analysis). Click a bar to see its items.
  • Malware by type, CVEs by exploitation risk and Threat actors by type.
  • Notable recent items (severity 30 and above), next to Items per source and IOC verdicts.

Every chart and list counts stories the same way. Only Items per source counts each outlet's copies, because it describes what each outlet published. The details are in Counting rules.

docs.title: Tables and preview
docs.text:
The Feed, IOC, Malware, Threat actor and CVE lists all share one table design: sortable headers that stay visible while you scroll, a bold main column with a second line and a row of related entities, the same period filter (24 hours to 1 year, or all time), a button to clear the filters, and pagination.

New threats. The Malware, Threat actors, CVEs and IOCs lists, and the Scam types and Impersonated brands lists, have a ✦ New threats button next to the filters. It keeps only the entries first seen within the chosen period, so you can see what has just appeared rather than what is always in the news. When the period is All time, it uses the last 30 days (7 days on the IOC list). Your other filters stay as they are, and clicking the button again (New threats ✕) or Reset shows everything.

Feed filters stay until you clear them. On the Feed, the filters you pick are kept for your session. Choosing a language after a minimum severity keeps the severity, and coming back to the Feed later shows the same view. The search box in the top bar and the entity chips only change the filter they name. Filters that a link set (an entity, a target country or province, a reporting country) appear as chips under the filter bar; click the ✕ on one to drop just that filter. Clear filters drops them all and starts over. The other lists keep their filters in the URL and have a Reset button.

Clicking a title opens a side preview with the essentials: the severity breakdown, the AI summary, indicators and their verdicts (with the date of each verdict), provider results and related items. Use ↑ / ↓ (or j / k) to move to the previous or next row, and Esc to close it. Full page opens the detail page in a new tab, and you can share the URL (?preview=item:12) with a colleague. Ctrl-click, Cmd-click or a middle click still open the page itself.

Copies. When several outlets carry the same article, the first one is the original and the others are copies. The Feed lists each story once and tells you how many copies it left out; tick Show copies to list them too, marked with a copy badge. On an item's page and in its preview, a copy says "Copy of …", and the original says "Also carried by N other outlets".

Indicator verdicts. Every verdict shows the date it was last given or confirmed ("verdict as of …"). An IP, domain or URL whose malicious verdict hasn't been confirmed for 60 days is marked aged and left out of the export feeds until a provider confirms it again (see Verdicts that age).

docs.title: Sources and enrichment at a glance
docs.text:
• Source health. On the Sources tab (Settings → Sources), each source shows when it last brought in a new item, how many it brought this week compared with usual, how long it has been failing, and whether its feed only carries short summaries. Sources that need attention are listed above the table. See Source health.
  • Enrichment queue and quotas. The IOC page (for analysts and admins) and Settings → Enrichment show how many indicators are waiting to be looked up, whether the job is keeping up, and how much of each provider's daily budget has been used. On the IOC page this is the Enrichment panel above the filters; click it to open the details. Run enrichment batch starts a run straight away, and Copy visible copies the indicators shown in the table, one per line. See The queue.

docs.title: Correcting JATMP
docs.text:
Analysts and admins can fix the platform's mistakes, and the fix stays in force:

  • ✕ next to an entity on an item page removes it from that item ("Pegasus" in an article about a musical).
  • ✎ Correct on an entity page marks a family or actor as a wrong entity everywhere, an indicator as not a threat, or sets an analyst verdict (malicious, suspicious, clean) that wins over the providers.
  • Not a scam report in the fraud-score popover of an item.

Each asks for a reason. The Corrections page lists them all with who, when and why, can undo any of them, and shows which names are corrected most often (rules worth tuning). Details in Corrections and quality.

docs.title: Job status and notifications
docs.text:
Under Collect now and Enrich now, the dashboard shows when each job last ran and when it runs next. While a job is running, you see a live progress bar ("Collecting… 12/50 sources · 8 new"), and the button stays disabled until the run finishes.

The bell in the top bar collects the results:

  • one summary per manual collection ("Collected 42 new items from 50 sources, 2 errors");
  • sources that start failing, have been failing for a day, or have gone quiet;
  • failed enrichment runs;
  • a provider's daily quota being used up;
  • the AI executive summary being ready.

Notifications are kept for 30 days.

docs.title: How JATMP works
docs.text:
This section explains what JATMP does behind the scenes. Every automatic process is described in the order it happens, together with the rules and numbers it uses.

It is written for three kinds of readers:

  • Analysts who want to know where a score, a verdict or a trend comes from before they rely on it.
  • Administrators who tune sources, quotas and schedules.
  • Anyone who wants to check that the platform behaves the way they expect.

If you are looking for the code structure, see Architecture; for the tables and columns, see Data model. These pages describe behaviour.

Everything here is rule-based and deterministic: the same input always gives the same result, and every score lists its reasons on the item page. The optional AI features can add to those results, but only within fixed limits, and they never replace them (see AI processing).

docs.title: The five stages
docs.text:
Every piece of information in JATMP goes through the same five stages.

Stage What happens When Read more 1. Collect Each enabled source fetches whatever its provider currently lists On the source's own interval (at least every 5 minutes); also on Collect now and during a Backfill Collection 2. Ingest and analyse New entries are de-duplicated, cleaned, searched for entities, scored for severity and fraud, tagged with sectors and geography, and stored Straight away, inside the collection run Ingest and analysis, Severity scoring, Scams and fraud 3. Enrich Indicators are looked up on the intel providers you configured, and their answers are combined into one verdict Every 10 minutes, 8 indicators at a time (the defaults) Enrichment and verdicts 4. All five stages run inside one process: the web application with its built-in scheduler (see Architecture). There is no queue between the stages, so by the time a collection run finishes, every item it found has been fully analysed.

docs.title: Follow one article through JATMP
docs.text:
The easiest way to understand the platform is to follow a single item from start to finish. The article below is made up, but every number in this walkthrough was produced by running its text through JATMP's own code.

LockBit ransomware exploits Citrix zero-day to hit Indonesian hospitals

Researchers say a new LockBit campaign is actively exploited in the wild against hospitals in Jakarta and Surabaya. The flaw, CVE-2026-31337, allows remote code execution on unpatched appliances. The operators used the T1190 technique. Indicators: 185.220.101[.]54, update-citrix[.]net, hxxps://update-citrix[.]net/payload.exe. Rumah sakit di Jakarta mengalami gangguan layanan.

docs.title: Collection (t = 0)
docs.text: The outlet's RSS source comes up on its schedule. JATMP downloads the feed (up to 10 MB), reads up to 500 entries, applies the source's topic filter if it has one, and passes the newest 100 to the pipeline. → Collection

docs.title: Ingest (a few milliseconds later)
docs.text:
Still inside the same run, the article goes through these steps:

  1. Is it new? JATMP hasn't stored this entry from this source before, so it carries on.
  2. Clean-up. HTML, scripts and any stray stylesheet text are removed. The link is kept because it starts with https://.
  3. Is it a syndicated copy? A fingerprint of the normalised title is compared with articles from other sources over the last four days. Nothing matches, so this item is the original.

  4. Entities. The extractor finds six:

    Type Value Origin Why it counts malware LockBit (ransomware) kb It is in the knowledge base cve CVE-2026-31337 regex Matches the CVE pattern technique T1190 regex Matches the ATT&CK id pattern ip 185.220.101.54 regex A public IPv4 address, written defanged domain update-citrix.net regex Written defanged ([.]). News is read in strict mode, where only defanged hosts count url https://update-citrix.net/payload.exe regex Restored from hxxps://…[.]…

  5. Severity. The points add up to 132, which is capped at 100. They come from: zero-day in the title (30 × 1.5 = 45), "exploited in the wild" as the runner-up in the same group (15), remote code execution (14), ransomware in the title (18), an active campaign (10), a sensitive sector as runner-up (4), a known family (10), one CVE (5), three indicators (8) and an ATT&CK technique (3). → Severity scoring

  6. Fraud. The text describes no scam, so the fraud score is 0. The item is not a scam report.
  7. Sectors. "hospitals" in the title and rumah sakit in the body make it a health sector item.
  8. Geography. The language is English. "Indonesian" in the title plus Jakarta and Surabaya in the body make Indonesia the target country (score 8.25), with the provinces DKI Jakarta and Jawa Timur.
  9. Links. All seven entities (the six above plus the sector) are linked to the item, and each entity's mention count and first-seen / last-seen dates are updated.

docs.title: Right after the commit (under a second)
docs.text: The trend cache is cleared, so the dashboard includes the item the next time someone opens it. A severity of 100 is above the default webhook threshold of 70, so an item.high_severity event is queued for every webhook that subscribes to it. If MISP auto-push is on, a push job is queued too, and if AI auto-summaries are on, the item joins the summary queue.

docs.title: Enrichment (within 10 minutes)
docs.text: None of the three indicators has been looked up yet, and this item has the highest severity in the queue, so they are among the next ones checked. Each configured provider answers. Suppose VirusTotal reports the IP as malicious: the combined verdict becomes malicious, every item that mentions the IP gets +12 indicator confirmed malicious (this one is already at 100), and an ioc.malicious webhook event is queued. The IP's page shows "verdict as of" today's date. → Enrichment and verdicts

docs.title: CVE intel (within 6 hours)
docs.text: CVE-2026-31337 is looked up in CISA KEV, FIRST EPSS and the NVD. If it turns out to be in KEV, its trend score on the dashboard is doubled. → Trends and correlation

docs.title: Every time someone opens the dashboard
docs.text: LockBit's trend score counts this article as one story. If five outlets syndicate it, it still counts once: the feed shows it a single time, and the item page lists the other outlets that carried it. The National (ID) view includes the item because it targets Indonesia.

docs.title: 30 seconds later
docs.text: The webhook delivery job sends the queued events. → Sharing and delivery

docs.title: 30 days later
docs.text: If the IP has been mentioned in the last 90 days, JATMP looks it up again, because addresses change hands. If the providers no longer flag it, the verdict goes down and the bonus is taken off the items that mention it. If nobody confirms it within 60 days, it drops out of the IOC export feeds. → Verdicts that age

docs.title: 180 days later
docs.text: The nightly housekeeping slims the item. The title, link, entities, scores and a 400-character snippet are kept; the full text is removed. → Housekeeping and re-analysis

docs.title: A day on the scheduler
docs.text:
These are the default timings. Most can be changed under Settings. The two daily jobs run at a local time in the time zone you choose under Settings → General; the defaults are UTC.

When Job What it does 5 s, 8 s, 11 s … after start-up First run of each source Sources start at 5 s + 3 s × source id, so they don't all hit the network at once 15 s after start-up run_content_cleanup Cleans stored text again if the cleaning rules changed (otherwise does nothing) 20 s after start-up run_geotag Re-tags geography if the rules changed 30 s after start-up run_dedup Fingerprints stored articles if the dedup rules changed 40 s after start-up run_fraudtag Re-runs the scam analysis if the rules changed 60 s after start-up run_sectortag Re-tags sectors if the rules changed 75 s after start-up run_digesttag Flags newsletters and round-ups if the rules changed 90 s after start-up run_rescore_if_outdated Re-scores stored items if the severity rules changed 2 min after start-up, then every 10 min run_enrichment Looks up 8 indicators, plus re-checks, aged verdicts and 2 trending families when enabled; each provider works at its own pace 3 min after start-up, then every 6 h run_cve_intel Fetches KEV, EPSS and CVSS for up to 60 recently mentioned CVEs 15 min after start-up, then hourly run_source_health Warns about sources that went quiet or keep failing Every 30 s run_webhooks Delivers up to 50 webhook events that are due Every 30–180 min, per source run_source Collects and ingests one source 03:30 daily (housekeeping_time) run_housekeeping Removes old runs, notifications and deliveries; slims old items; deletes them if you enabled that; prunes scammer identifiers 06:00 daily (digest_time) run_digest Writes the AI executive summary (when an AI model is configured and the summary is on) 04:00 UTC on the 5th of each month run_geoip_update Refreshes the offline GeoIP database (when auto-update is on) 2 s after new items arrive run_auto_summaries Writes AI summaries for new items with severity ≥ 40 (when enabled), 10 per run

Two scheduler rules apply to every job. A job that is still running when its next turn comes is not started a second time, and runs that were missed while the process was busy or stopped are merged into one (as long as they are no more than 10 minutes late). All jobs share a pool of 10 threads.

It rises by +12 / +5 when an indicator is later confirmed malicious or suspicious, and by up to +20 from the AI Severity scoring Fraud score (0–100) The scam analysis, when the item is stored. 0 means "not a scam report" Scams and fraud Verdict on an indicator, and its date The combined answer of the enrichment providers, with the date it was last given or confirmed. docs.title: Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning Source One configured feed, account, channel or intel query, with its own collector type, interval and sharing rules Item One stored article, post, pulse, scan or analysis. Every item belongs to exactly one source Story An original item together with its syndicated copies. Dashboards count stories, so a story carried by five outlets counts once Entity Anything JATMP tracks across items: a malware family, threat actor, CVE, ATT&CK technique, indicator, scam type, brand, scammer identifier or sector. Each one is unique by its type and normalised value Link A record that says "this item mentions this entity", together with how it was found (its origin): regex, kb, heuristic, feed or llm Indicator (IOC) An entity of type ip, domain, url, md5, sha1 or sha256 Verdict JATMP's combined opinion on an indicator: malicious, suspicious, clean or unknown, or empty if it hasn't been checked successfully yet. It always comes with the date it was last given or confirmed Run One execution of a job, recorded with its status Batch The runs started by one manual action (Collect now, Backfill). They share one progress bar and one summary notification Live / backfill Whether an item was collected as it appeared, or fetched from history later Original / copy When another outlet publishes the same article within four days, the later one is a copy of the first Slimmed An item older than the full-text retention period. Its text is cut to a snippet; everything else stays Rules version A number in the code that goes up whenever detection or scoring rules change. When it differs from the version stored in the database, a one-off job re-analyses the stored items Correction An analyst's fix of a mistake: a wrong entity on one item or everywhere, an analyst verdict, or "not a scam report". It has a reason and an author, stays in force when JATMP re-analyses, and can be undone

docs.title: What JATMP does not do
docs.text:
Knowing the limits helps you read the results correctly.

  • It only reads what the source delivers. For RSS, that is the text inside the feed entry; JATMP does not open the article page. Feeds that only carry a short summary produce fewer entities, and the Sources tab marks them as summary only.
  • It never visits leak sites or criminal infrastructure. Leak-site victims come from the ransomware.live aggregator, and indicators are looked up on intel providers rather than contacted directly.
  • It never looks up scammer identifiers anywhere. Bank accounts and wallets get links so an analyst can check them by hand.
  • It doesn't use machine learning. Detection is based on rules, vocabularies and a knowledge base. A language model only runs if you configure the optional AI, and what it can change is limited. Analysts' corrections fix individual cases and show which rules need tuning, but JATMP doesn't change its rules by itself.
  • It doesn't re-run entity extraction on its own. When a new version changes the scoring, fraud, sector, geography or cleaning rules, stored items are re-analysed automatically once. Changes to entity extraction only reach old items when you run manage.py reextract (see Housekeeping and re-analysis).
